vocab.def_en: To make someone feel embarrassed, disconcerted, or ill at ease
vocab.quote_en: The titter that rippled around the room appeared to abash the boy, but in reality that result was caused rather more by his worshipful awe of his unknown idol and the dread pleasure that lay in his high good fortune.
vocab.quote_zh: 教室里响起的窃笑声似乎让那男孩感到尴尬，但实际上，这种感觉更多是由于他对那不知名的偶像的敬畏，以及他因这意外的好运而产生的既害怕又快乐的心情。
vocab.ex_en: True confidence needs no armor, but the abashed soul often builds walls where bridges should stand.
vocab.ex_zh: 真正的自信不需要盔甲，但尴尬的灵魂常常在应该搭建桥梁的地方筑起高墙。

vocab.def_en: To remain; to stay; to tolerate or endure
vocab.quote_en: At last luck seemed to settle and abide with Joe.
vocab.quote_zh: 最后，运气似乎稳定下来，留在了乔这边。
vocab.ex_en: Those who cannot abide solitude will never discover the strength that silence teaches.
vocab.ex_zh: 无法忍受孤独的人永远发现不了寂静所教给他们的力量。

vocab.def_en: To be plentiful or numerous; to exist in large quantities
vocab.quote_en: His pity was moved, but nevertheless he felt an abounding sense of relief and security, now, which revealed to him in a degree which he had not fully appreciated before, how vast a weight of dread had been lying upon him since the day he lifted his voice against this bloody-minded outcast.
vocab.quote_zh: 他的同情心被触动了，但他仍然感到一种强烈的解脱和安全感，这让他前所未有地意识到，自从那天他指证这个残忍的被遗弃者以来，一直压在他心头的恐惧是多么巨大。
vocab.ex_en: Where curiosity abounds, learning follows like a faithful shadow.
vocab.ex_zh: 好奇心旺盛的地方，学习就如忠实的影子紧随其后。

vocab.def_en: Wildly unreasonable, illogical, or inappropriate; ridiculous
vocab.quote_en: He worshipped this new angel with furtive eye, till he saw that she had discovered him; then he pretended he did not know she was present, and began to show off in all sorts of absurd boyish ways, in order to win her admiration.
vocab.quote_zh: 他偷偷地崇拜着这个新来的天使，直到发现她注意到了自己；然后他假装不知道她在场，开始用各种荒唐可笑的男孩方式炫耀自己，想赢得她的赞赏。
vocab.ex_en: The absurd is not always foolish; sometimes it is wisdom wearing a jester's cap.
vocab.ex_zh: 荒谬不一定愚蠢;有时候它是戴着丑角帽的智慧。

vocab.def_en: To approach and speak to someone boldly or aggressively
vocab.quote_en: At the door Tom dropped back a step and accosted a Sunday-dressed comrade.
vocab.quote_zh: 在门口，汤姆落后一步，上前跟一个穿着礼拜日服装的同伴搭话。
vocab.ex_en: To accost a stranger is to open a door; what lies beyond is always a gamble.
vocab.ex_zh: 与陌生人搭话就是打开一扇门;门后是什么永远是一场赌博。

vocab.def_en: Unbreakable; unyielding; firm in purpose
vocab.def_zh: 坚定不移的;坚硬的;不屈的
vocab.quote_en: He got home pretty late that night, and when he climbed cautiously in at the window, he uncovered an ambuscade, in the person of his aunt; and when she saw the state his clothes were in, her resolution to turn his Saturday holiday into captivity at hard labor became adamantine in its firmness.
vocab.quote_zh: 那天晚上他很晚才回家，当他小心翼翼地从窗户爬进去时，发现了姨妈设下的埋伏；当她看到他的衣服变成那副样子时，她要把他的周六假期变成强制劳役的决心变得坚定不移。
vocab.ex_en: The human spirit, though fragile in appearance, often possesses an adamantine core that suffering itself cannot crack.
vocab.ex_zh: 人类的精神虽然外表脆弱，却常常拥有苦难本身也无法摧毁的坚定不移的内核。

vocab.def_en: A follower or supporter of a person, party, or cause
vocab.quote_en: He gathered quite a following of lads interested in the exhibition; and one that had cut his finger and had been a center of fascination and homage up to this time, now found himself suddenly without an adherent, and shorn of his glory.
vocab.quote_zh: 他吸引了一群对这项表演感兴趣的男孩；而一个之前因为割伤手指而一直备受关注和崇拜的男孩，现在突然发现自己一个追随者也没有了，风光也被剥夺了。
vocab.ex_en: Truth needs no adherents to be true, but it gathers them like flowers turning toward the sun.
vocab.ex_zh: 真理不需要拥护者才成为真理，但它会吸引拥护者，就像花朵朝向太阳。

vocab.def_en: To make more beautiful or attractive; to decorate
vocab.quote_en: A sumptuous breakfast of bacon and fish was shortly provided, and as the boys set to work upon it, Tom recounted (and adorned) his adventures.
vocab.quote_zh: 很快，一顿由熏肉和鱼组成的丰盛早餐就准备好了，当男孩们开始享用时，汤姆讲述（并添油加醋地装饰）了他的冒险经历。
vocab.ex_en: Kindness adorns the soul more elegantly than any jewel could ever adorn the body.
vocab.ex_zh: 善良装饰灵魂，比任何珠宝装饰身体都更加优雅。

vocab.def_en: Brisk and cheerful readiness; eager willingness
vocab.quote_en: Tom gave up the brush with reluctance in his face but alacrity in his heart.
vocab.quote_zh: 汤姆脸上带着不情愿，心里却乐开了花，把刷子递了出去。
vocab.ex_en: Fortune favors not the hesitant but those who seize opportunity with alacrity.
vocab.ex_zh: 命运眷顾的不是犹豫不决的人，而是那些欣然抓住机会的人。

vocab.def_en: A metal made by combining two or more metallic elements; something that detracts from value when mixed
vocab.quote_en: His exaltation had but one alloy—the memory of his humiliation in this angel's garden—and that record in sand was fast washing out under the waves of happiness that were sweeping over it now.
vocab.quote_zh: 他的狂喜只有一点瑕疵——在这个天使的花园里受辱的记忆——而那个沙上的印记正被此刻席卷而来的幸福浪潮迅速冲刷殆尽。
vocab.ex_en: Fear is the alloy in the gold of courage, present in small measure even in the bravest heart.
vocab.ex_zh: 恐惧是勇气这枚金币中的杂质，即使是最勇敢的心里也有一点点。

vocab.def_en: Strong hostility or hatred
vocab.quote_en: She thrust it away again, but with less animosity.
vocab.quote_zh: 她又把它推开，但敌意已经没那么强烈了。
vocab.ex_en: Animosity is a poison we drink expecting others to die.
vocab.ex_zh: 仇恨是我们喝下期待别人死去的毒药。

vocab.def_en: The action of anticipating something; expectation or prediction
vocab.quote_en: Ben's gait was the hop-skip-and-jump—proof enough that his heart was light and his anticipations high.
vocab.quote_zh: 本的步态是三级跳——这足以证明他心情轻松，期望很高。
vocab.ex_en: Anticipation is the mind's dress rehearsal for joys and sorrows yet to come.
vocab.ex_zh: 预期是心灵为未来的欢乐与悲伤进行的彩排。

vocab.def_en: Lack of interest, enthusiasm, or concern
vocab.def_zh: 冷漠;漠不关心;无动于衷
vocab.quote_en: She had sunk into a dreary apathy and would not be roused.
vocab.quote_zh: 她陷入了可怕的冷漠之中，无法被唤醒。
vocab.ex_en: Apathy is the soul's winter, when nothing grows and even hope sleeps beneath the frost.
vocab.ex_zh: 冷漠是灵魂的冬天，万物不生，连希望也在霜冻下沉睡。

vocab.def_en: Anxious or fearful about the future; uneasy
vocab.quote_en: There was something in the tone that made Tom apprehensive.
vocab.quote_zh: 那语气里有什么东西让汤姆感到不安。
vocab.ex_en: The apprehensive heart sees shadows where none exist and hears footsteps in every whisper of the wind.
vocab.ex_zh: 忧虑的心在无影处看见阴影，在风声里听见脚步。

vocab.def_en: In a manner that shows anxiety or fear about the future
vocab.quote_en: They glanced backward over their shoulders from time to time apprehensively, as if they feared they might be followed.
vocab.quote_zh: 他们不时回头张望，忧心忡忡，好像害怕有人追赶他们似的。
vocab.ex_en: Those who walk apprehensively through life miss the flowers at their feet, their eyes fixed only on distant clouds.
vocab.ex_zh: 忧心忡忡地走过人生的人，眼睛只盯着远方的云，错过了脚下的花朵。

vocab.def_en: The highest class in certain societies, typically comprising people of noble birth
vocab.def_zh: 贵族;贵族阶级;上层社会
vocab.quote_en: "Any other boy in the whole town but that Saint Louis smarty that thinks he dresses so fine and is aristocracy!"
vocab.quote_zh: "除了那个自以为穿得好、是贵族的圣路易斯臭美家伙，镇上哪个男孩都行！"
vocab.ex_en: True aristocracy is not of blood but of character.
vocab.ex_zh: 真正的贵族不是血统的贵族，而是品格的贵族。

vocab.def_en: To agree to a proposal, request, or view
vocab.quote_en: "Oh, don't, Tom, it is too horrid," said Becky. "It is horrid, but I better, Becky; they might hear us, you know," and he shouted again. Amy chatted happily along as they walked, for her heart was singing, but Tom's tongue had lost its function. He did not hear what Amy was saying, and whenever she paused expectantly he could only stammer an awkward assent, which was as often misplaced as otherwise.
vocab.quote_zh: "哦，别叫了，汤姆，太可怕了，"贝姬说。"是可怕，但我最好再叫，贝姬；你知道，他们也许能听见我们，"他又叫了一声。艾米在他们走路时开心地聊着，因为她的心在歌唱，但汤姆的舌头已经失去了功能。他没听见艾米在说什么，每当她期待地停下来时，他只能结结巴巴地表示尴尬的同意，而且常常是答非所问。
vocab.ex_en: Wisdom lies not in giving assent to every opinion, but in choosing carefully which truths to embrace.
vocab.ex_zh: 智慧不在于同意每一个观点，而在于谨慎选择接受哪些真理。

vocab.def_en: To succeed in achieving something; to reach
vocab.quote_en: [Note: This word does not appear in the novel. Using a thematically appropriate sentence.] Tom believed that by becoming a pirate, he would attain the freedom and glory he dreamed of.
vocab.quote_zh: 汤姆相信，通过成为一名海盗，他将获得他所梦想的自由和荣耀。
vocab.ex_en: The heights by great men reached and kept were not attained by sudden flight, but they, while their companions slept, were toiling upward in the night.
vocab.ex_zh: 伟人达到并保持的高度并非一蹴而就，而是在同伴们酣睡时，他们仍在黑夜中奋力向上攀登。

vocab.def_en: The process of gradually weakening or wearing down
vocab.quote_en: But the incidents of his adventure grew sensibly sharper and clearer under the attrition of thinking them over, and so he presently found himself leaning to the impression that the thing might not have been a dream, after all.
vocab.quote_zh: 但是，在反复思考的琢磨下，他冒险经历中的细节变得越来越清晰，于是他很快发现自己倾向于认为这件事毕竟可能不是梦。
vocab.ex_en: Character is not formed by sudden revelation but by the slow attrition of daily choices.
vocab.ex_zh: 品格不是由突然的启示形成的，而是由日常选择的缓慢磨砺形成的。

vocab.def_en: Showing a willingness to take surprisingly bold risks
vocab.quote_en: You been into some other audacious mischief when I wasn't around, like enough.
vocab.quote_zh: 我不在的时候，你八成又闯了什么别的胆大包天的祸。
vocab.ex_en: Fortune favors the audacious, but wisdom tempers audacity with care.
vocab.ex_zh: 命运眷顾大胆的人，但智慧用谨慎调和胆量。

vocab.def_en: Able to be heard
vocab.quote_en: His whisper was hardly audible when he said: "Oh, Huck, it's a stray dog!"
vocab.quote_zh: 当他用几乎听不见的耳语说"哦，哈克，是条野狗！"时，声音小得几乎听不见。
vocab.ex_en: The most important truths are often barely audible, whispered by conscience in moments of quiet.
vocab.ex_zh: 最重要的真理常常几乎听不见，是良心在安静时刻低语的。

vocab.def_en: An audience; a group of listeners
vocab.quote_en: Tom lay upon a sofa with an eager auditory about him and told the history of the wonderful adventure.
vocab.quote_zh: 汤姆躺在沙发上，周围围着一群热切的听众，讲述着那次奇妙冒险的经历。
vocab.ex_en: Every soul craves an auditory for its story; we are all narrators seeking listeners.
vocab.ex_zh: 每个灵魂都渴望有人倾听自己的故事；我们都是寻找听众的叙述者。

vocab.def_en: Respected and impressive; majestic
vocab.def_zh: 威严的;令人敬畏的;庄严的
vocab.quote_en: The middle-aged man turned out to be a prodigious personage: no less a one than the county judge—altogether the most august creation these children had ever looked upon.
vocab.quote_zh: 那个中年人原来是个了不起的大人物：正是县法官本人——完全是这些孩子们见过的最威严的人物。
vocab.ex_en: Time renders all things humble that once seemed august, yet memory preserves their majesty.
vocab.ex_zh: 时间让一切曾经威严的事物变得谦卑，但记忆保存了它们的庄严。

vocab.def_en: A divine or prophetic token; patronage or guidance
vocab.quote_en: Here was treasure-hunting under the happiest auspices—there would not be any bothersome uncertainty as to where to dig.
vocab.quote_zh: 这是在最幸运的预兆下进行的寻宝活动——对于在哪里挖掘不再有任何烦人的不确定性。
vocab.ex_en: Under the auspices of hope, even the most daunting journey becomes possible.
vocab.ex_zh: 在希望的庇佑下，即使是最艰巨的旅程也变得可能。

vocab.def_en: Conducive to success; favorable
vocab.quote_en: Everything was auspicious.
vocab.quote_zh: 一切都很顺利。
vocab.ex_en: Beginnings are auspicious not by chance but by the alignment of preparation with opportunity.
vocab.ex_zh: 开端吉利不是偶然的，而是准备与机遇的结合。

vocab.def_en: In a greedy manner; with an insatiable desire for wealth
vocab.quote_en: One day Tom was in the act of dosing the crack when his aunt's yellow cat came along, purring, eyeing the teaspoon avariciously, and begging for a taste.
vocab.quote_zh: 一天，汤姆正在给裂缝喂药，他姨妈的黄猫走过来，咕噜咕噜地叫着，贪婪地盯着茶匙，讨要一口尝尝。
vocab.ex_en: The eye that looks avariciously upon the world sees only what it covets, never what it has.
vocab.ex_zh: 贪婪地看世界的眼睛只看到它觊觎的东西，永远看不到它拥有的东西。

vocab.def_en: A person's regular occupation or main job
vocab.quote_en: The majority of the searchers had given up the quest and gone back to their daily avocations.
vocab.quote_zh: 大多数搜寻者已经放弃了寻找，回到了他们的日常工作中。
vocab.ex_en: One's avocation may pay the bills, but one's vocation calls the soul.
vocab.ex_zh: 职业可能支付账单，但天职召唤灵魂。

vocab.def_en: To turn away or prevent something from happening
vocab.quote_en: And now and then they stooped in a group and splashed water in each other's faces with their palms, gradually approaching each other, with averted faces to avoid the strangling sprays.
vocab.quote_zh: 他们不时地聚成一团，用手掌往彼此脸上泼水，慢慢地互相靠近，把脸转开以避开呛人的水花。
vocab.ex_en: Courage does not always roar; sometimes it is the quiet voice at the end of the day saying, "I will try again tomorrow."
vocab.ex_zh: 勇气并不总是咆哮；有时它是夜深人静时轻声说："我明天再试一次。"

vocab.def_en: In a manner that is menacing or harmful; ominously
vocab.quote_en: He was now become, to them, the most balefully interesting object they had ever looked upon, and they could not take their fascinated eyes from his face.
vocab.quote_zh: 现在，对他们来说，他变成了他们见过的最邪恶又最令人着迷的对象，他们无法把着迷的目光从他的脸上移开。
vocab.ex_en: The past may look balefully upon us, but we choose whether to meet its gaze or turn toward the future.
vocab.ex_zh: 过去可能凶恶地注视着我们，但我们可以选择是迎接它的目光还是转向未来。

vocab.def_en: Late or delayed; happening after the expected time
vocab.quote_en: And it was said that a belated citizen had come upon Potter washing himself in the "branch" about one or two o'clock in the morning.
vocab.quote_zh: 据说，一个晚归的市民在凌晨一两点钟撞见波特在"小溪"里洗澡。
vocab.ex_en: A belated apology, sincerely offered, can still mend what time has broken.
vocab.ex_zh: 迟来的道歉，如果真诚地给出，仍然可以修补时间所破坏的东西。

vocab.def_en: A beautiful woman or girl, especially the most attractive one in a particular place
vocab.def_zh: 美女;美人;最迷人的女子
vocab.quote_en: Next the belle of the village, followed by a troop of lawn-clad and ribbon-decked young heart-breakers.
vocab.quote_zh: 接下来是村子的美女，后面跟着一群身穿细麻布衣服、扎着缎带的令人心动的年轻姑娘。
vocab.ex_en: Every age has its belles, but true beauty outlasts the admiration of any single season.
vocab.ex_zh: 每个时代都有自己的美女，但真正的美丽比任何一个季节的赞美都更持久。

vocab.def_en: The utterance of a blessing, especially at the end of a religious service
vocab.def_zh: 祝福;恩赐;(礼拜结束时的)赐福祈祷
vocab.quote_en: The sun rose upon a tranquil world, and beamed down upon the peaceful village like a benediction.
vocab.quote_zh: 太阳升起在宁静的世界，像祝福一样照耀着平静的村庄。
vocab.ex_en: A kind word can be a benediction to a weary soul.
vocab.ex_zh: 一句善意的话可以成为对疲惫灵魂的祝福。

vocab.def_en: Characterized by large waves; swelling or surging like waves
vocab.def_zh: 波涛汹涌的;波浪般的;起伏的
vocab.quote_en: Under the ceaseless conflagration of lightning that flamed in the skies, everything below stood out in clean-cut and shadowless distinctness: the bending trees, the billowy river, white with foam.
vocab.quote_zh: 在天空中不断燃烧的闪电下，下方的一切都清晰无影地凸显出来：弯曲的树木，波涛汹涌的河流，泛着白色的泡沫。
vocab.ex_en: Life's journey is a billowy sea, but every wave carries us closer to shore.
vocab.ex_zh: 人生的旅程是波涛汹涌的大海，但每一波浪潮都把我们带得更靠近岸边。

vocab.def_en: To become pale from fear, shock, or illness
vocab.quote_en: "What is it?" whispered Huck, blanching with fright.
vocab.quote_zh: "怎么回事？"哈克低声说，吓得脸色发白。
vocab.ex_en: Truth may blanch the cheek, but it fortifies the soul.
vocab.ex_zh: 真理可能让脸颊苍白，但它能坚固灵魂。

vocab.def_en: Spoiled, ruined, or destroyed; affected by decay
vocab.def_zh: 被毁坏的;枯萎的;受摧残的
vocab.quote_en: And thus she would see him when she looked out upon the glad morning, and oh! would she drop one little tear upon his poor, lifeless form, would she leave one little sigh to see a bright young life so rudely blighted, so untimely cut down?
vocab.quote_zh: 这样，当她看向欢快的早晨时，她会看到他，哦！她会不会在他可怜的、没有生气的身体上滴一滴眼泪，会不会轻轻叹息，看到一个灿烂的年轻生命如此粗鲁地被摧残，如此过早地夭折？
vocab.ex_en: A blighted hope is not a dead hope; it is merely hope learning to grow in different soil.
vocab.ex_zh: 被摧残的希望不是死的希望；它只是希望学习在不同的土壤中生长。

vocab.def_en: A feeling of evil to come; an omen
vocab.quote_en: Then he took the kite-line in his hand and went groping down one of the passages on his hands and knees, distressed with hunger and sick with bodings of coming doom.
vocab.quote_zh: 然后他拿起风筝线，用手和膝盖摸索着走下其中一条通道，因饥饿而痛苦，因对即将来临的厄运的预感而恶心。
vocab.ex_en: Boding thoughts are the mind's warning system; heed them, but do not let them paralyze you.
vocab.ex_zh: 不祥的预感是心灵的预警系统；注意它们，但不要让它们麻痹你。

vocab.def_en: Noisy, energetic, and cheerful; rough and stormy
vocab.quote_en: Even the boisterous winds unanimously came forth from their mystic homes, and blustered about as if to enhance by their aid the wildness of the scene.
vocab.quote_zh: 甚至连狂暴的风也从它们神秘的家园中一齐涌出，呼啸着，仿佛要用它们的力量来增强场景的狂野。
vocab.ex_en: Beneath every boisterous exterior often beats a heart that knows its own quiet depths.
vocab.ex_zh: 在每个喧闹的外表下，常常跳动着一颗知道自己安静深处的心。

vocab.def_en: A picture, description, or imitation of a person in which certain striking characteristics are exaggerated
vocab.def_zh: 漫画;讽刺画;夸张的描述
vocab.quote_en: Tom partly uncovered a dismal caricature of a house with two gable ends to it and a cork-screw of smoke issuing from the chimney.
vocab.quote_zh: 汤姆部分露出一幅阴郁的房子漫画，房子有两座山墙，烟囱里冒出一缕螺旋状的烟。
vocab.ex_en: Memory is a caricature artist, exaggerating our joys and diminishing our sorrows until the past becomes almost bearable.
vocab.ex_zh: 记忆是个漫画家，夸大我们的快乐，缩小我们的悲伤，直到过去变得几乎可以忍受。

vocab.def_en: An event causing great and often sudden damage or suffering; a disaster
vocab.quote_en: But they found there was still something to be thankful for, because the great sycamore, the shelter of their beds, was a ruin, now, blasted by the lightnings, and they were not under it when the catastrophe happened.
vocab.quote_zh: 但他们发现仍然有值得庆幸的事情，因为那棵为他们遮风挡雨的大梧桐树现在已被雷电击毁，而灾难发生时他们并没有在树下。
vocab.ex_en: Every catastrophe carries within it the seed of renewal, waiting for the right season to sprout.
vocab.ex_zh: 每一场灾难内部都携带着更新的种子，等待合适的季节发芽。

vocab.def_en: A shrill howling or wailing noise, like that of a cat
vocab.quote_en: And then there came, mingling with his half-formed dreams, a most melancholy caterwauling.
vocab.quote_zh: 然后，在他半成形的梦中，传来一阵最凄凉的猫叫春声。
vocab.ex_en: The caterwauling of the world's discord often drowns out the still, small voice within.
vocab.ex_zh: 世界不和谐的刺耳叫声常常淹没了内心那安静、微小的声音。

vocab.def_en: Irritation or annoyance; the state of being rubbed sore
vocab.quote_en: Tom had been restless and full of chafings and repinings; conscience-smitten, too—he could not meet Amy Lawrence's eye, he could not brook her loving gaze.
vocab.quote_zh: 汤姆一直坐立不安，充满烦躁和懊恼；也良心不安——他不敢看艾米·劳伦斯的眼睛，无法忍受她爱怜的目光。
vocab.ex_en: The chafing of small irritations can wear down the soul more than any single great sorrow.
vocab.ex_zh: 小小烦恼的摩擦比任何一次巨大的悲伤更能磨损灵魂。

vocab.def_en: A deep fissure in the earth's surface; a profound difference between people or viewpoints
vocab.quote_en: Some boards were soon uncovered and removed. They had concealed a natural chasm which led under the rock.
vocab.quote_zh: 很快，一些木板被揭开并移走。它们掩盖了一条通向岩石下面的天然裂缝。
vocab.ex_en: Between intention and action lies a chasm that only will can bridge.
vocab.ex_zh: 在意图和行动之间横亘着一道只有意志才能跨越的鸿沟。

vocab.def_en: A loud and confused noise, especially of people shouting
vocab.quote_en: The moment a candle was lighted there was a general rush upon the owner of it; a struggle and a gallant defence followed, but the candle was soon knocked down or blown out, and then there was a glad clamor of laughter and a new chase.
vocab.quote_zh: 蜡烛一点亮，大家就都冲向拿着它的人；接着是一场挣扎和英勇的防守，但蜡烛很快就被打翻或吹灭，然后是一阵欢快的笑声喧闹和新的追逐。
vocab.ex_en: In the clamor of competing voices, wisdom listens for the one that speaks truth quietly.
vocab.ex_zh: 在 competing 声音的喧嚣中，智慧倾听那个安静说出真理的声音。

vocab.def_en: Loud and confused; making a loud and often sustained noise
vocab.quote_en: He sprung his secret about Huck's share in the adventure in the finest dramatic manner he was master of, but the surprise it occasioned was largely counterfeit and not as clamorous and effusive as it might have been under happier circumstances.
vocab.quote_zh: 他以他掌握的最好的戏剧性方式透露了关于哈克在这次冒险中的贡献的秘密，但它引起的惊喜很大程度上是虚假的，不像在更快乐的情况下可能那么喧闹和热情洋溢。
vocab.ex_en: The clamorous demand attention, but the worthy earn it silently.
vocab.ex_zh: 喧闹的人要求关注，但有价值的人默默地赢得关注。

vocab.def_en: In a secret or covert manner, especially with reference to something forbidden or improper
vocab.def_zh: 秘密地;私下地;偷偷摸摸地
vocab.quote_en: If it had been Sid, she would have had no misgivings to alloy her delight; but since it was Tom, she watched the bottle clandestinely.
vocab.quote_zh: 如果是希德，她的快乐就不会有任何疑虑掺杂其中；但因为是汤姆，她就偷偷地监视着药瓶。
vocab.ex_en: Truth, when it must be sought clandestinely, often proves more valuable than truth freely offered.
vocab.ex_zh: 当真理必须秘密寻找时，它往往比自由提供的真理更有价值。

vocab.def_en: Extremely large; enormous
vocab.def_zh: 巨大的;庞大的; colossal sigh 巨大的叹息
vocab.quote_en: He unrolled it. A long, lingering, colossal sigh followed, and his heart broke.
vocab.quote_zh: 他把它展开。随后是一声长长的、持续的、巨大的叹息，他的心碎了。
vocab.ex_en: A colossal dream requires an equally colossal commitment to realize it.
vocab.ex_zh: 巨大的梦想需要同样巨大的承诺才能实现。

vocab.def_en: To think deeply about something; to ponder
vocab.quote_en: Then they separated, cogitating.
vocab.quote_zh: 然后他们分开了，各自沉思着。
vocab.ex_en: The mind that learns to cogitate in solitude gains strength for the battles of the marketplace.
vocab.ex_zh: 学会在孤独中沉思的心灵，为市场的战斗获得力量。

vocab.def_en: Something given as payment or recompense for loss, injury, or suffering
vocab.quote_en: But all trials bring their compensations.
vocab.quote_zh: 但所有的磨难都会带来补偿。
vocab.ex_en: The universe has its own arithmetic; every loss carries within it the seed of compensation.
vocab.ex_zh: 宇宙有自己的算术；每一个损失内部都携带着补偿的种子。

vocab.def_en: Made up of various parts or elements
vocab.quote_en: [Note: This word appears in the Preface of the book, not in the main chapters, but it is a key word from the author about Tom's character.] Tom was a composite character, drawn from three boys the author knew.
vocab.quote_zh: 汤姆是个复合型人物，由作者认识的三男孩的特征综合而成。
vocab.ex_en: Every soul is composite, built from fragments of those we've loved and places we've been.
vocab.ex_zh: 每个灵魂都是复合体，由我们爱过的人和去过的地方的碎片构建而成。

vocab.def_en: To act in a way that shows one feels superior to others; to lower oneself
vocab.def_zh: 俯就;屈尊;表现出优越感
vocab.quote_en: These two great commanders did not condescend to fight in person—that being better suited to the still smaller fry.
vocab.quote_zh: 这两位了不起的指挥官不屑于亲自参战——那更适合那些更小的孩子们。
vocab.ex_en: To condescend is to build a wall between yourself and others, mistaking height for connection.
vocab.ex_zh: 屈尊俯就是在自己与他人之间筑起一道墙，误以为高度就是连接。

vocab.def_en: A large, destructive fire
vocab.quote_en: and he knew of old that this insect was credulous about conflagrations, and he had practiced upon its simplicity more than once.
vocab.quote_zh: 他早就知道这种昆虫对火灾很轻信，而且他不止一次利用过它的单纯。
vocab.ex_en: A single spark of kindness can prevent the conflagration of despair.
vocab.ex_zh: 一点善良的火花就能防止绝望的大火。

vocab.def_en: To cause surprise or confusion; to mix up; used as a mild oath
vocab.def_zh: 使困惑;使惊讶;混淆;该死
vocab.quote_en: "She'd never noticed if it hadn't been for Sid. Confound it! sometimes she sews it with white, and sometimes she sews it with black."
vocab.quote_zh: "要不是希德，她根本不会注意到。该死！有时候她用白线缝，有时候用黑线缝。"
vocab.ex_en: Those who confound expectations are the ones who change the world.
vocab.ex_zh: 那些让人意想不到的人，才是改变世界的人。

vocab.def_en: To form an opinion or supposition based on incomplete information; to guess
vocab.quote_en: He went on listening, and gathered by odds and ends that it was conjectured at first that the boys had got drowned while taking a swim.
vocab.quote_zh: 他继续听着，从零星的谈话中了解到，起初人们猜测男孩们是在游泳时淹死的。
vocab.ex_en: Conjecture is the mind's attempt to paint pictures in the dark, hoping one stroke might capture truth.
vocab.ex_zh: 推测是心灵在黑暗中作画，希望某一笔能捕捉到真相。

vocab.def_en: Standing out so as to be clearly visible; attracting notice or attention
vocab.def_zh: 显眼的;引人注目的;突出的
vocab.quote_en: But after listening to Tom, he conceded that there were some conspicuous advantages about a life of crime, and so he consented to be a pirate.
vocab.quote_zh: 但听了汤姆的话后，他承认犯罪生活有一些显著的优势，于是他同意成为一名海盗。
vocab.ex_en: Virtue should be conspicuous not for praise, but as a lamp that lights the way for others.
vocab.ex_zh: 美德应该显眼不是为了得到赞美，而是作为照亮他人道路的灯。

vocab.def_en: Feelings of anxiety or dismay, typically at something unexpected
vocab.quote_en: This phase filled the old lady's heart with consternation.
vocab.quote_zh: 这个阶段让老太太心里充满了惊愕。
vocab.ex_en: Consternation is the mind's brief surrender to the unexpected before courage rallies its forces.
vocab.ex_zh: 惊愕是心灵在勇气重整旗鼓之前向意外的短暂投降。

vocab.def_en: Forced; unnatural; restricted
vocab.def_zh: 被迫的;不自然的;受约束的
vocab.quote_en: But the elastic heart of youth cannot be compressed into one constrained shape long at a time.
vocab.quote_zh: 但年轻人有弹性的心不能长时间被压缩成一个受约束的形状。
vocab.ex_en: The heart constrained by fear never learns to fly.
vocab.ex_zh: 被恐惧束缚的心永远学不会飞翔。

vocab.def_en: To interpret or understand in a particular way
vocab.quote_en: She judged that this would be construed into a confession that she had been in the wrong, and discipline forbade that.
vocab.quote_zh: 她判断这会被理解为承认自己错了，而纪律不允许这样做。
vocab.ex_en: We construe the world not as it is, but as we are.
vocab.ex_zh: 我们理解世界不是按照它本来的样子，而是按照我们自己的样子。

vocab.def_en: To look thoughtfully for a long time; to consider
vocab.quote_en: A log raft in the river invited him, and he seated himself on its outer edge and contemplated the dreary vastness of the stream.
vocab.quote_zh: 河里的一个木筏吸引了他，他坐在它的外缘，凝视着河流沉闷的广阔。
vocab.ex_en: To contemplate the stars is to measure not their distance but the depth of our own wonder.
vocab.ex_zh: 凝视星星，测量的是我们自己的惊奇有多深，而不是星星的距离有多远。

vocab.def_en: Showing scorn; disdainful
vocab.quote_en: A contemptuous smile flitted across Injun Joe's face.
vocab.quote_zh: 一丝轻蔑的微笑掠过印第安人乔的脸。
vocab.ex_en: The contemptuous look wounds the giver more than the receiver, for it hardens the heart that offers it.
vocab.ex_zh: 轻蔑的眼神伤害给予者比接受者更深，因为它使给予者的心变得坚硬。

vocab.def_en: To plan with cleverness; to scheme; to manage to do something
vocab.quote_en: Tom contrived to scarify the cupboard with it, and was arranging to begin on the bureau, when he was called off to dress for Sunday school.
vocab.quote_zh: 汤姆设法用它划伤了碗柜，正准备开始对付衣柜时，被叫去换衣服上主日学校。
vocab.ex_en: We contrive elaborate plans, but fate laughs at our blueprints and builds according to its own design.
vocab.ex_zh: 我们精心策划，但命运嘲笑我们的蓝图，按自己的设计建造。

vocab.def_en: Recovering from illness; in the process of regaining health
vocab.quote_en: At last he was pronounced upon the mend, and then convalescent.
vocab.quote_zh: 最后他被宣布正在好转，然后进入恢复期。
vocab.ex_en: The convalescent sees the world anew, as if born again into familiar yet strangely fresh surroundings.
vocab.ex_zh: 康复中的人重新看世界，仿佛重生在熟悉却又陌生地新鲜的环境中。

vocab.def_en: A person's face or facial expression
vocab.quote_en: Whispers passed along, and a boding uneasiness took possession of every countenance.
vocab.quote_zh: 低语声四处传开，一种不祥的不安占据了每个人的面容。
vocab.ex_en: The countenance is a mirror that reflects the soul's weather.
vocab.ex_zh: 面容是反映灵魂天气的镜子。

vocab.def_en: To yearn to possess something belonging to another
vocab.quote_en: He had discovered a great law of human action, without knowing it—namely, that in order to make a man or a boy covet a thing, it is only necessary to make the thing difficult to attain.
vocab.quote_zh: 他无意中发现了一个人类行为的伟大法则——那就是，要让一个大人或一个孩子渴望得到某样东西，只需要让这样东西难以获得。
vocab.ex_en: To covet is to build a prison for oneself, with walls made of others' possessions.
vocab.ex_zh: 觊觎就是为自己建一座监狱，墙壁由他人的财产筑成。

vocab.def_en: Too ready to believe things; easily convinced
vocab.def_zh: 轻信的;易信的;容易受骗的
vocab.quote_en: and he knew of old that this insect was credulous about conflagrations, and he had practiced upon its simplicity more than once.
vocab.quote_zh: 他早就知道这种昆虫对火灾很轻信，而且他不止一次利用过它的单纯。
vocab.ex_en: The credulous heart opens doors that wisdom would keep locked.
vocab.ex_zh: 轻信的心会打开智慧本应锁着的门。

vocab.def_en: In a state of mental confusion caused by fever; wildly excited
vocab.def_zh: 神志不清的;说胡话的;极度兴奋的
vocab.quote_en: He found Huck still in the bed that had been provided for him, and delirious with fever.
vocab.quote_zh: 他发现哈克还在为他准备的那张床上，因发烧而神志不清。
vocab.ex_en: Hope can make us delirious with joy, but despair's delirium is silence.
vocab.ex_zh: 希望能使我们兴奋得说胡话，但绝望的胡话是沉默。

vocab.def_en: A severe flood; a great downpour
vocab.quote_en: The window went up, a maid-servant's discordant voice profaned the holy calm, and a deluge of water drenched the prone martyr's remains!
vocab.quote_zh: 窗子拉了上去，一个女用人不和谐的声音亵渎了眼前这神圣的宁静，一大盆水兜头而下，打湿了平卧在地上的烈士的遗体！
vocab.ex_en: Kindness is a deluge that drowns the fires of hatred.
vocab.ex_zh: 善良是淹没仇恨之火的洪水。

vocab.def_en: Contemptuous ridicule or mockery
vocab.quote_en: The new boy took two broad coppers out of his pocket and held them out with derision.
vocab.quote_zh: 新来的男孩从口袋里掏出两个大铜板，带着嘲笑递给他。
vocab.ex_en: Derision is the weapon of those who have no argument.
vocab.ex_zh: 嘲弄是没有道理的人使用的武器。

vocab.def_en: The exercise of absolute power, especially in a cruel and oppressive way
vocab.quote_en: for the oppressed millions groaning under the heel of European monarchies and Oriental despotisms.
vocab.quote_zh: 为在欧洲君主制度和东方专制的铁蹄下呻吟的受压迫的百万民众。
vocab.ex_en: Despotism begins not in palaces but in hearts that have forgotten how to question.
vocab.ex_zh: 专制不是从宫殿开始，而是从忘记了如何质疑的心中开始。

vocab.def_en: Modest or shy because of lack of self-confidence
vocab.def_zh: 缺乏自信的;胆怯的;羞怯的
vocab.quote_en: "Speak out, my boy—don't be diffident. The truth is always respectable."
vocab.quote_zh: "说出来，我的孩子——别胆怯。真相总是值得尊敬的。"
vocab.ex_en: The diffident soul holds treasures the confident never seek.
vocab.ex_zh: 缺乏自信的灵魂拥有自信者从不寻觅的珍宝。

vocab.def_en: In a state of disrepair or ruin as a result of age or neglect
vocab.def_zh: 破旧的;破烂的;年久失修的
vocab.quote_en: and a dilapidated old window-sash.
vocab.quote_zh: 和一个破旧的旧窗框。
vocab.ex_en: A dilapidated house may still shelter dreams more beautiful than any palace.
vocab.ex_zh: 破旧的房子仍能庇护比任何宫殿都更美丽的梦想。

vocab.def_en: Careful and persistent work or effort
vocab.quote_en: Diligence and attention soon gave him the knack of it.
vocab.quote_zh: 勤奋和专注很快就让他掌握了窍门。
vocab.ex_en: Diligence is the bridge between dreams and their fulfillment.
vocab.ex_zh: 勤奋是梦想与其实现之间的桥梁。

vocab.def_en: In a way that shows careful and persistent effort
vocab.quote_en: He went outside the door and set the basin on a little bench there; then he dipped the soap in the water and laid it down; turned up his sleeves; poured out the water on the ground, gently, and then entered the kitchen and began to wipe his face diligently on the towel behind the door.
vocab.quote_zh: 他走到门外，把盆放在一条小长凳上；然后把肥皂浸在水里放下；卷起袖子；轻轻地把水倒在地上，然后走进厨房，开始在门后的毛巾上勤奋地擦脸。
vocab.ex_en: Time spent diligently in pursuit of worthy goals is never wasted, even when the goal remains elusive.
vocab.ex_zh: 勤奋追求有价值目标所花的时间永远不会浪费，即使目标仍然难以捉摸。

vocab.def_en: To make weaker by adding something else
vocab.quote_en: And then she diluted the compliment by adding, "But it's powerful seldom you're a mind to, I'm bound to say."
vocab.quote_zh: 然后她补充道，冲淡了这句赞扬，"但我得说，你很少有这样的心思。"
vocab.ex_en: Fear dilutes courage, but courage undiluted is recklessness.
vocab.ex_zh: 恐惧稀释勇气，但不稀释的勇气是鲁莽。

vocab.def_en: Disturbed or agitated; made uneasy or embarrassed
vocab.quote_en: Tom was a trifle disconcerted.
vocab.quote_zh: 汤姆有点尴尬。
vocab.ex_en: The truth, when first encountered, often leaves us disconcerted, for it rarely matches our expectations.
vocab.ex_zh: 初次遭遇真相时，它常常让我们困惑，因为它很少符合我们的预期。

vocab.def_en: Harsh and unpleasant in sound; disagreeing or incongruous
vocab.def_zh: 刺耳的;不和谐的;不一致的
vocab.quote_en: The window went up, a maid-servant's discordant voice profaned the holy calm.
vocab.quote_zh: 窗子拉了上去，一个女用人不和谐的声音亵渎了眼前这神圣的宁静。
vocab.ex_en: Discordant notes in music resolve into harmony; so too do discordant moments in life, given time.
vocab.ex_zh: 音乐中的不和谐音会化解为和谐;生活中的不和谐时刻也是如此，假以时日。

vocab.def_en: Depressing; dreary; causing gloom or misery
vocab.def_zh: 阴郁的;沉闷的;令人沮丧的
vocab.quote_en: He wandered far from the accustomed haunts of boys, and sought desolate places that were in harmony with his spirit. A log raft in the river invited him, and he seated himself on its outer edge and contemplated the dreary vastness of the stream, wishing, the while, that he could only be drowned, all at once and unconsciously, without undergoing the uncomfortable routine devised by nature. Then he thought of his flower. He got it out, rumpled and wilted, and it mightily increased his dismal felicity.
vocab.quote_zh: 他远离男孩们常去的地方，寻找与他的心情相配的孤寂的地方。河里的一个木筏吸引了他，他坐在它的外缘，凝视着河流沉闷的广阔，同时巴不得自己能被淹死，一下子就死过去，而不要经历那个由大自然设计的令人难受的过程。这时他想到了他的花儿。他把花拿出来，花儿已经被压皱，枯萎，这更大大地增加了他那种阴郁的幸福感。
vocab.ex_en: Even the most dismal night eventually yields to dawn.
vocab.ex_zh: 即使是最阴郁的夜晚，最终也会让位于黎明。

vocab.def_en: The instruction or improvement of a person morally or intellectually
vocab.quote_en: No matter what the subject might be, a brain-racking effort was made to squirm it into some aspect or other that the moral and religious mind could contemplate with edification.
vocab.quote_zh: 无论主题是什么，都要绞尽脑汁把它扭曲成某种道德和宗教思想可以沉思以获得启迪的方面。
vocab.ex_en: True edification comes not from being told what to think, but from learning how to think.
vocab.ex_zh: 真正的启迪不是被告知该想什么，而是学会如何思考。

vocab.def_en: A large, imposing building
vocab.quote_en: the edifice was but a small, plain affair, with a sort of pine board tree-box on top of it for a steeple.
vocab.quote_zh: 这座建筑只是个小而普通的房子，顶上有个松木板做的树箱当尖顶。
vocab.ex_en: An edifice of lies, however grand, will crumble at the first touch of truth.
vocab.ex_zh: 谎言的大厦无论多么宏伟，在真理的第一次触碰下就会坍塌。

vocab.def_en: Having qualities traditionally associated with women; not manly
vocab.def_zh: 女人气的;柔弱的;娘娘腔的
vocab.quote_en: He privately smoothed out the curls, with labor and difficulty, and plastered his hair close down to his head; for he held curls to be effeminate, and his own filled his life with bitterness.
vocab.quote_zh: 他私底下费劲地把鬈发撸直，抹上发油，让头发紧贴着头皮；他向来觉得鬈发女里女气的，他自己的鬈发就使他的生活充满痛苦。
vocab.ex_en: Strength wears no single face; the effeminate heart may harbor courage that muscle-bound men have never known.
vocab.ex_zh: 力量没有单一的面孔;女人气的心中可能蕴藏着肌肉发达的男人从未知晓的勇气。

vocab.def_en: An unrestrained expression of feelings
vocab.quote_en: The prize was delivered to Tom with as much effusion as the superintendent could pump up under the circumstances.
vocab.quote_zh: 校长尽其所能地带着感情把奖品颁给了汤姆。
vocab.ex_en: Emotional effusion, like rain, can nourish or flood; wisdom lies in knowing when to open the gates.
vocab.ex_zh: 感情的倾泻如同雨水，既能滋养也能泛滥;智慧在于知道何时开闸。

vocab.def_en: Expressing feelings in an unrestrained, heartfelt way
vocab.def_zh: 感情奔放的;热情洋溢的;溢于言表的
vocab.quote_en: but the surprise it occasioned was largely counterfeit and not as clamorous and effusive as it might have been under happier circumstances.
vocab.quote_zh: 但它引起的惊喜很大程度上是虚假的，不像在更快乐的情况下可能那么喧闹和热情洋溢。
vocab.ex_en: An effusive welcome can warm the coldest heart, but sincerity must fuel its fire.
vocab.ex_zh: 热情洋溢的欢迎能温暖最冰冷的心，但真诚必须是其燃料。

vocab.def_en: To pass by (of time)
vocab.quote_en: He thought all this and more in the moment that elapsed between the stranger's remark and Injun Joe's next.
vocab.quote_zh: 他在陌生人说完话和印第安人乔接着说话之间的那一刻里想到了所有这些，甚至更多。
vocab.ex_en: Time may elapse slowly in suffering and swiftly in joy, yet its measure is the same.
vocab.ex_zh: 时间在痛苦中流逝得慢，在欢乐中流逝得快，但它的度量是一样的。

vocab.def_en: Fluent or persuasive in speaking or writing; vividly expressive
vocab.def_zh: 雄辩的;有口才的;富于表情的
vocab.quote_en: At school the children made so much of him and of Joe, and delivered such eloquent admiration from their eyes, that the two heroes were not long in becoming insufferably "stuck-up."
vocab.quote_zh: 在学校里，孩子们对他和乔大加赞赏，眼神中流露出如此富有表现力的钦佩，以至于这两位英雄很快就变得令人难以忍受的"自命不凡"。
vocab.ex_en: The most eloquent speech is sometimes a silence that speaks volumes.
vocab.ex_zh: 最雄辩的演讲有时是无声胜有声。

vocab.def_en: A decorative detail or feature added to make something more attractive
vocab.quote_en: When you talked about notching ears and slitting noses I judged that that was your own embellishment, because white men don't take that sort of revenge.
vocab.quote_zh: 当你谈到割耳朵和割鼻子时，我以为那是你自己的添油加醋，因为白人不采取那种报复方式。
vocab.ex_en: Truth needs no embellishment, but stories often do, and so does love.
vocab.ex_zh: 真理不需要修饰，但故事常常需要，爱情也是如此。

vocab.def_en: A position of prominence or superiority; a high place
vocab.quote_en: These two great commanders did not condescend to fight in person—that being better suited to the still smaller fry—but sat together on an eminence and conducted the field operations by orders delivered through aides-de-camp.
vocab.quote_zh: 这两位了不起的指挥官不屑于亲自参战——那更适合那些更小的孩子们——而是并肩坐在一个高地上，通过副官传达命令来指挥战斗。
vocab.ex_en: Eminence is not a destination but a vantage point from which to serve.
vocab.ex_zh: 卓越不是目的地，而是服务的有利位置。

vocab.def_en: To provide with a quality, ability, or asset
vocab.quote_en: Like many other simple-hearted souls, it was her pet vanity to believe she was endowed with a talent for dark and mysterious diplomacy.
vocab.quote_zh: 像许多头脑简单的人一样，她有一种特别的虚荣心，相信自己天生就有耍弄神秘莫测手段的天赋。
vocab.ex_en: Nature endows each soul with unique gifts; the tragedy is how often they remain unopened.
vocab.ex_zh: 大自然赋予每个灵魂独特的礼物;悲剧在于它们常常未被打开。

vocab.def_en: To settle securely or comfortably
vocab.quote_en: They found the sharp new heap they were seeking, and ensconced themselves within the protection of three great elms that grew in a bunch within a few feet of the grave.
vocab.quote_zh: 他们找到了他们正在寻找的那个新的尖坟头，把自己安顿在离坟墓几英尺远的三棵挤在一起的大榆树的保护下。
vocab.ex_en: The heart that ensconces itself too safely never learns to dance.
vocab.ex_zh: 把自己安顿得太安全的心，永远学不会跳舞。

vocab.def_en: Soon passing out of sight, memory, or existence; fleeting
vocab.def_zh: 短暂的;转瞬即逝的;易消散的
vocab.quote_en: He had thought he loved her to distraction; he had regarded his passion as adoration; and behold it was only a poor little evanescent partiality.
vocab.quote_zh: 他曾经以为他爱她爱得发狂；他曾经把自己的这种激情看作是一种崇拜；谁知这只是种可怜的、短暂的偏爱。
vocab.ex_en: Beauty is evanescent, but the memory of beauty can last a lifetime.
vocab.ex_zh: 美是短暂的，但对美的记忆可以持续一生。

vocab.def_en: To cough or spit out phlegm from the throat or lungs
vocab.quote_en: He gathered quite a following of lads interested in the exhibition; and one that had cut his finger and had been a center of fascination and homage up to this time, now found himself suddenly without an adherent, and shorn of his glory. His heart was heavy, and he said with a disdain which he did not feel that it wasn't anything to spit like Tom Sawyer; but another boy said, "Sour grapes!" and he wandered away a dismantled hero. [Note: "expectorate" itself does not appear; the word "spit" is used.]
vocab.quote_zh: 他吸引了一群对这项表演感兴趣的男孩；而一个之前因为割伤手指而一直备受关注和崇拜的男孩，现在突然发现自己一个追随者也没有了，风光也被剥夺了。他的心沉甸甸的，用不屑的口气说，他认为像汤姆这样吐痰根本算不了什么；但另一个男孩说："酸葡萄！"他就像个失意英雄似的走开了。
vocab.ex_en: Words, once expectorated, can never be swallowed again.
vocab.ex_zh: 话说出口，就像痰吐出去，再也收不回来。

vocab.def_en: The act of spitting; matter that is coughed up and spat out
vocab.quote_en: The silences widened; the expectoration marvelously increased.
vocab.quote_zh: 沉默的间隔变长了；吐痰量惊人地增加了。
vocab.ex_en: Expectoration clears the lungs; confession clears the soul.
vocab.ex_zh: 吐痰清肺，忏悔清魂。

vocab.def_en: A feeling of triumphant elation or jubilation
vocab.def_zh: 狂喜;欢欣鼓舞;得意洋洋
vocab.quote_en: He was in such ecstasies that he even controlled his tongue and was silent. He said to himself that he would not speak a word, even when his aunt came in, but would sit perfectly still till she asked who did the mischief; and then he would tell, and there would be nothing so good in the world as to see that pet model "catch it." He was so brimful of exultation that he could hardly hold himself when the old lady came back and stood above the wreck discharging lightnings of wrath from over her spectacles.
vocab.quote_zh: 他欣喜若狂，以至于控制住舌头，一言不发。他对自己说，就算姨妈进来他也不说话，而是静静地坐着，直到她问是谁闯的祸；然后他就会说出来，世界上没有什么比看到那个宠儿"受罚"更让他高兴的了。他心中充满了狂喜，当老太太回来站在碎片上方，从眼镜上方射出愤怒的闪电时，他几乎控制不住自己。
vocab.ex_en: Exultation in another's misfortune is a joy that poisons the one who feels it.
vocab.ex_zh: 对他人不幸的狂喜是一种毒害感受者自身的快乐。

vocab.def_en: Treating serious issues with deliberately inappropriate humor; joking
vocab.def_zh: 滑稽的;轻浮的;爱开玩笑的
vocab.quote_en: The discourse was resumed presently, but it went lame and halting, all possibility of impressiveness being at an end; for even the gravest sentiments were constantly being received with a smothered burst of unholy mirth, under cover of some remote pewback, as if the poor parson had said a rarely facetious thing.
vocab.quote_zh: 布道不一会儿又继续了下去，但已变得有气无力，吞吞吐吐，给人以随时可能结束的印象；就连最严肃的祝愿语，会众们在听的时候也是靠着前面长椅的掩护，强压着渎神的欢笑，好像那可怜的牧师说的是一个难得的滑稽事情。
vocab.ex_en: The facetious tongue often speaks truths that solemn lips dare not utter.
vocab.ex_zh: 轻浮的舌头常常说出庄严的嘴唇不敢说的真相。

vocab.def_en: To suffer or cause to suffer from extreme hunger
vocab.quote_en: how the men didn't believe the wild tale at first, "because," said they, "you are five miles down the river below the valley the cave is in"; then took them aboard, rowed to a house, gave them supper, made them rest till two or three hours after dark, and then brought them home. Before day-dawn, Judge Thatcher and the handful of searchers with him were tracked out, in the cave, by the twine clues they had strung behind them, and informed of the great news. Three days and nights of toil and hunger in the cave were not to be shaken off at once, as Tom and Becky soon discovered. They were bedridden all of Wednesday and Thursday, and seemed to grow more and more tired and worn all the time. Tom got about, a little, on Thursday, was downtown Friday, and nearly as whole as ever Saturday; but Becky did not leave her room until Sunday, and then she looked as if she had passed through a wasting illness.
vocab.quote_zh: 那些人起初不相信这个荒唐的故事，"因为，"他们说，"那个岩洞是在山谷里，而你们是在河下游五英里的地方"；然后他们让汤姆和贝姬上了船，划到一座屋子，给他们吃了晚饭，让他们休息到天黑后两三个小时，然后带他们回了家。天亮前，派去送信的人们在岩洞里根据撒切尔法官和一帮搜寻者撒下的缠绕的绳子找到了他们，把这个天大的消息告诉了他们。汤姆和贝姬很快就发现，岩洞里三天三夜的劳累和饥饿并不是一下子就能恢复过来的。
vocab.ex_en: The soul that famishes for beauty will feast on a single flower.
vocab.ex_zh: 渴求美的灵魂，一朵花就能让它饱餐。

vocab.def_en: Intense happiness; the ability to find appropriate expression for one's thoughts
vocab.quote_en: He wandered far from the accustomed haunts of boys, and sought desolate places that were in harmony with his spirit. A log raft in the river invited him, and he seated himself on its outer edge and contemplated the dreary vastness of the stream, wishing, the while, that he could only be drowned, all at once and unconsciously, without undergoing the uncomfortable routine devised by nature. Then he thought of his flower. He got it out, rumpled and wilted, and it mightily increased his dismal felicity.
vocab.quote_zh: 他远离男孩们常去的地方，寻找与他的心情相配的孤寂的地方。河里的一个木筏吸引了他，他坐在它的外缘，凝视着河流沉闷的广阔，同时巴不得自己能被淹死，一下子就死过去，而不要经历那个由大自然设计的令人难受的过程。这时他想到了他的花儿。他把花拿出来，花儿已经被压皱，枯萎，这更大大地增加了他那种阴郁的幸福感。
vocab.ex_en: Felicity is not found in having much, but in wanting little and appreciating all.
vocab.ex_zh: 幸福不在于拥有很多，而在于想要很少并感激一切。

vocab.def_en: To prevent or obstruct by taking action ahead of time
vocab.def_zh: 预先阻止;抢先一步;预防
vocab.quote_en: But in spite of her, Tom knew where the wind lay, now. So he forestalled what might be the next move.
vocab.quote_zh: 但是尽管如此，汤姆现在已经知道了她的用意。于是他抢先一步，阻止了她可能的下一步行动。
vocab.ex_en: To forestall regret, act with kindness before the moment passes.
vocab.ex_zh: 要预防后悔，就在时机过去之前行善。

vocab.def_en: To paint on wet plaster; a painting done on plaster
vocab.quote_en: Still drifting along and talking, they scarcely noticed that they were now in a part of the cave whose walls were not frescoed.
vocab.quote_zh: 他们仍然一边漂流一边说话，几乎没有注意到他们现在已经到了岩洞的一个墙壁上没有壁画的地方。
vocab.ex_en: Memory frescoes our minds with images time cannot wash away.
vocab.ex_zh: 记忆用时间无法洗去的图像在我们的脑海中作画。

vocab.def_en: Lack of seriousness; lighthearted fun
vocab.quote_en: For frivolity and jokes and spotted tights were an offense when they intruded themselves upon a spirit that was exalted into the vague august realm of the romantic.
vocab.quote_zh: 因为当一个人的精神升华到令人隐约感到敬畏的浪漫王国时，轻薄的举动、玩笑的话语和花里胡哨的紧身衣裤再要闯进来，那就是一种冒犯了。
vocab.ex_en: A little frivolity is the soul's permission to breathe between the weights of duty.
vocab.ex_zh: 一点轻浮是灵魂在责任的重量之间允许自己呼吸。

vocab.def_en: Having the mournful, somber character appropriate to a funeral
vocab.quote_en: There was no whispering in the house; only the funereal rustling of dresses, as the women gathered to their seats, disturbed the silence there.
vocab.quote_zh: 教堂里没有窃窃私语；只有女人们落座时衣服发出的葬礼般的窸窣声打破了那里的沉寂。
vocab.ex_en: The funereal mood that follows loss eventually gives way to the bright dawn of memory.
vocab.ex_zh: 失去之后的悲哀情绪最终会让位于记忆的明亮曙光。

vocab.def_en: Attempting to avoid notice or attention; secretive
vocab.def_zh: 偷偷摸摸的;鬼鬼祟祟的;秘密的
vocab.quote_en: He worshipped this new angel with furtive eye, till he saw that she had discovered him.
vocab.quote_zh: 他偷偷地崇拜着这个新来的天使，直到发现她注意到了自己。
vocab.ex_en: Love's first steps are often furtive, afraid of its own reflection.
vocab.ex_zh: 爱情的最初几步常常是偷偷摸摸的，害怕看到自己的影子。

vocab.def_en: A person's manner of walking
vocab.quote_en: Ben's gait was the hop-skip-and-jump—proof enough that his heart was light and his anticipations high.
vocab.quote_zh: 本的步态是三级跳——这足以证明他心情轻松，期望很高。
vocab.ex_en: The gait reveals what words conceal: joy dances, sorrow drags, purpose strides.
vocab.ex_zh: 步态揭示言语隐藏的东西：快乐跳跃，悲伤拖沓，目标大步。

vocab.def_en: To make sore by rubbing; to irritate or annoy
vocab.quote_en: He now looked exceedingly improved and uncomfortable. He was fully as uncomfortable as he looked; for there was a restraint about whole clothes and cleanliness that galled him.
vocab.quote_zh: 他现在看起来大为改善，但也极不舒服。他完全像看上去那样不舒服；因为全身干净的衣服和整洁让他感到束缚和恼火。
vocab.ex_en: Small injustices gall more than great ones, for they are constant companions.
vocab.ex_zh: 小的不公比大的更让人烦恼，因为它们是常伴。

vocab.def_en: A top-floor or attic room
vocab.quote_en: There was a garret above, pierced with a scuttle over his head; and down through this scuttle came a cat, suspended around the haunches by a string.
vocab.quote_zh: 那里有一个阁楼，他头顶上方有一个天窗；一只猫从这天窗里被放下来，腰腿部绑着一根绳子。
vocab.ex_en: Dreams born in a garret often soar higher than those born in palaces.
vocab.ex_zh: 阁楼里诞生的梦想常常比宫殿里诞生的飞得更高。

vocab.def_en: Friendly and cheerful; pleasantly warm
vocab.quote_en: So soft was her step, it failed to make even a sound, and but for the magical thrill imparted by her genial touch, as other unobtrusive beauties, she would have glided away unperceived—unsought.
vocab.quote_zh: 她的脚步如此轻柔，几乎没有发出任何声响，要不是她亲切的触摸所带来的神奇般的激动，她会像其他不张扬的美人一样，飘然而过，不为人知——无人追随。
vocab.ex_en: A genial word can melt the frost that has gathered on another's heart.
vocab.ex_zh: 一句友好的话能融化聚集在别人心上的霜。

vocab.def_en: A vigorous motion or gesture
vocab.quote_en: A very little boy stood up and sheepishly recited, "You'd scarce expect one of my age to speak in public on the stage," etc., accompanying himself with the painfully exact and spasmodic gestures which a machine might have used—supposing the machine to be a trifle out of order.
vocab.quote_zh: 一个小男孩站了起来，怯生生地背诵道："你不太会想到一个像我这样年纪的人会在台上向公众讲话，"等等，伴随着背诵声的是异常精确的、抽风似的手势，像是用机器操纵似的——或许机器还出了点故障。
vocab.ex_en: Words are the body's language, but gesticulation is the soul's.
vocab.ex_zh: 言语是身体的语言，而手势是灵魂的语言。

vocab.def_en: To cover with a thin layer of gold
vocab.quote_en: And how the light did blaze abroad from the master's bald pate—for the sign-painter's boy had gilded it!
vocab.quote_zh: 老师的光脑袋多么光彩夺目啊——因为做招牌人的孩子已经给那脑袋镀了金！
vocab.ex_en: Time gilds memory, turning even painful moments into treasures of the heart.
vocab.ex_zh: 时间给记忆镀金，甚至把痛苦的时刻变成心中的珍宝。

vocab.def_en: Splendor and impressiveness, especially of appearance or style
vocab.quote_en: True, the knife would not cut anything, but it was a "sure-enough" Barlow, and there was inconceivable grandeur in that—though where the western boys ever got the idea that such a weapon could possibly be counterfeited to its injury is an imposing mystery and will always remain so, perhaps.
vocab.quote_zh: 不错，这把小刀切不了任何东西，但它却是一把"货真价实"的巴洛刀，拥有它就拥有了一种不可思议的气派——不过，西部的男孩子们从哪里得到这样的概念，认为这样的武器居然可能被仿冒，从而使它的声誉受到玷污，这是一个不同凡响的秘密，也许永远都是一个秘密。
vocab.ex_en: True grandeur lies not in what we have but in what we give.
vocab.ex_zh: 真正的宏伟不在于我们拥有什么，而在于我们给予什么。

vocab.def_en: Seriousness; importance
vocab.quote_en: The other boys agreed that there was reason in what Tom said, because an ignorant lump of bread, uninstructed by an incantation, could not be expected to act very intelligently when sent upon an errand of such gravity.
vocab.quote_zh: 其他孩子都承认汤姆说的有点道理，因为，假如一只无知的面包，没有被施过咒语，是无法指望它在执行一项如此重要的差使时做得这么聪明的。
vocab.ex_en: Humor without gravity is empty; gravity without humor is unbearable.
vocab.ex_zh: 没有严肃的幽默是空洞的;没有幽默的严肃是难以忍受的。

vocab.def_en: Sly or cunning intelligence
vocab.quote_en: While Tom was eating his supper, and stealing sugar as opportunity offered, Aunt Polly asked him questions that were full of guile and very deep—for she wanted to trap him into damaging revealments.
vocab.quote_zh: 当汤姆在吃晚饭，一有机会就偷吃一点糖的时候，波莉姨妈就开始盘问他，她的话里布满陷阱，而且很深——因为她要让他自己把做了什么坏事给说出来。
vocab.ex_en: Innocence has no defense against guile but experience.
vocab.ex_zh: 纯真对狡猾没有防御，除了经验。

vocab.def_en: To create difficulties for someone or something, resulting in delay or obstruction
vocab.quote_en: "Well, go 'long—who's hindering you."
vocab.quote_zh: "嗯，走吧——谁拦着你啦。"
vocab.ex_en: Fear hinders more journeys than any mountain ever could.
vocab.ex_zh: 恐惧阻碍的旅程比任何山都多。

vocab.def_en: Special honor or respect shown publicly
vocab.quote_en: He gathered quite a following of lads interested in the exhibition; and one that had cut his finger and had been a center of fascination and homage up to this time, now found himself suddenly without an adherent, and shorn of his glory.
vocab.quote_zh: 他吸引了一群对这项表演感兴趣的男孩；而一个之前因为割伤手指而一直备受关注和崇拜的男孩，现在突然发现自己一个追随者也没有了，风光也被剥夺了。
vocab.ex_en: True homage is paid not with words but with lives lived in honor of another.
vocab.ex_zh: 真正的敬意不是用言语表达的，而是用尊敬他人的生活表达的。

vocab.def_en: Past tense of heave; to have risen or appeared
vocab.quote_en: Ben Rogers hove in sight presently—the very boy, of all boys, whose ridicule he had been dreading.
vocab.quote_zh: 不一会儿，本·罗杰斯出现了——在那么多男孩子中，汤姆就怕被他嘲笑。
vocab.ex_en: When opportunity hove into view, the prepared mind recognizes it.
vocab.ex_zh: 当机会出现时，有准备的心能认出它。

vocab.def_en: Excessively critical; too quick to find fault
vocab.def_zh: 吹毛求疵的;苛刻的;过于挑剔的
vocab.quote_en: He was not much posted in anatomy, and not hypercritical, anyway.
vocab.quote_zh: 他对解剖学知之甚少，而且也不是个吹毛求疵的人。
vocab.ex_en: The hypercritical eye sees specks in others while missing the beam in its own.
vocab.ex_zh: 吹毛求疵的眼睛看到别人眼中有刺，却看不到自己眼中有梁木。

vocab.def_en: The state of being about to happen
vocab.quote_en: The very imminence of the emergency paralyzed his invention.
vocab.quote_zh: 紧急情况的迫近让他的机智瘫痪了。
vocab.ex_en: The imminence of loss teaches us the value of what we have.
vocab.ex_zh: 失去的迫近教会我们珍惜拥有的价值。

vocab.def_en: About to happen
vocab.quote_en: Then at once they reached and hovered upon the imminent verge of sleep—but an intruder came, now, that would not "down."
vocab.quote_zh: 接着他们很快就到达并徘徊在睡着的边缘——但是有一个东西闯了进来，赶也赶不走。
vocab.ex_en: When change is imminent, the wise prepare while the foolish resist.
vocab.ex_zh: 当变化迫近时，智者准备，愚者抵抗。

vocab.def_en: Protection or exemption from something
vocab.quote_en: Presently she stepped into the kitchen, and Sid, happy in his immunity, reached for the sugar-bowl.
vocab.quote_zh: 不一会儿她进了厨房，得到豁免权的希德高兴地伸手去拿糖碗。
vocab.ex_en: No one has immunity from the consequences of their choices.
vocab.ex_zh: 没有人能免于自己选择的后果。

vocab.def_en: The quality of being impertinent; disrespectful boldness
vocab.quote_en: "Infernal impudence!" said a bystander; "wanted to come and take a quiet look at his work, I reckon."
vocab.quote_zh: "简直死不要脸！"一个旁观者说；"我看他是想来悄悄看一看他干的好事。"
vocab.ex_en: Impudence is often the mask fear wears when it forgets itself.
vocab.ex_zh: 厚颜无耻常常是恐惧忘记自己时戴的面具。

vocab.def_en: In a manner that is not clearly expressed; without coherent speech
vocab.def_zh: 口齿不清地;表达不清地
vocab.quote_en: The doctor murmured inarticulately, gave a long gasp or two, and was still.
vocab.quote_zh: 医生口齿不清地咕哝着，长长地喘了一两口气，然后就没声儿了。
vocab.ex_en: Grief often speaks inarticulately, for words cannot contain its depth.
vocab.ex_zh: 悲伤常常表达不清，因为言语无法容纳它的深度。

vocab.def_en: A series of words said as a magic spell or charm
vocab.quote_en: He put his hand there and uttered this incantation impressively: "What hasn't come here, come! What's here, stay here!"
vocab.quote_zh: 他把手放上去，煞有介事地念起咒语："没有来的，来吧！已经来的，留下吧！"
vocab.ex_en: Love needs no incantation; its magic works in silence.
vocab.ex_zh: 爱情不需要咒语；它的魔力在沉默中发挥作用。

vocab.def_en: A person's natural tendency or urge to act or feel in a particular way
vocab.quote_en: The sure fun of the evening outweighed the uncertain treasure; and, boylike, he determined to yield to the stronger inclination and not allow himself to think of the box of money another time that day.
vocab.quote_zh: 当晚确定的乐趣比那笔没有把握的财宝更重要；像个男孩一样，他决定屈服于这个更强的诱惑，决不允许自己在那天再一次想到那个钱箱。
vocab.ex_en: To follow every inclination is to be blown about like a leaf; wisdom chooses which winds to sail.
vocab.ex_zh: 追随每一种倾向就像叶子随风飘荡；智慧选择乘风破浪。

vocab.def_en: Not in harmony or keeping with the surroundings; out of place
vocab.def_zh: 不协调的;不一致的;不合适的
vocab.quote_en: It might have seemed to him a waste of pomp and ammunition to kill a bug with a battery of artillery, but there seemed nothing incongruous about the getting up such an expensive thunder storm as this to knock the turf from under an insect like himself.
vocab.quote_zh: 用一组排炮去杀死一个小小的甲虫，这似乎是小题大做，浪费弹药，但是动用这样奢侈的雷暴来轰炸一个像他这样的虫子底下的草根土，似乎没有任何不合适的。
vocab.ex_en: The incongruous often catches our attention and teaches us to see anew.
vocab.ex_zh: 不协调的东西常常引起我们的注意，教我们重新看世界。

vocab.def_en: Certain to happen; unavoidable
vocab.def_zh: 不可避免的;必然发生的
vocab.quote_en: The switch hovered in the air—the peril was desperate—"My! Look behind you, aunt!" The old lady whirled round, and snatched her skirts out of danger. The lad fled on the instant, scrambled up the high board-fence, and disappeared over it.
vocab.quote_zh: 鞭子悬在空中——一顿暴抽在所难免——"哎呀！看你身后，姨妈！"老太太抽转身，一把抓住衣服的下摆以避开危险。孩子当即拔脚就溜，翻过高高的木板栅栏，没了身影。
vocab.ex_en: Change is inevitable, but growth is optional.
vocab.ex_zh: 变化是不可避免的，但成长是可选的。

vocab.def_en: Incapable of making mistakes or being wrong
vocab.def_zh: 绝对可靠的;永无过失的;万无一失的
vocab.quote_en: The truth was, that a superstition of his had failed here, which he and all his comrades had always looked upon as infallible.
vocab.quote_zh: 事实是，他的一个迷信在这里失败了，他和他的同伴们一直以为这是绝对可靠的。
vocab.ex_en: Only the foolish claim to be infallible; the wise know their own fallibility.
vocab.ex_zh: 只有傻瓜声称自己绝对可靠；智者知道自己的易错性。

vocab.def_en: Of or relating to hell; hateful; damnable
vocab.quote_en: "with those infernal boys playing over there on the hill right in full view."
vocab.quote_zh: "那些该死的男孩就在那边的山上玩，看得一清二楚。"
vocab.ex_en: Patience is the antidote to infernal irritation.
vocab.ex_zh: 耐心是对抗地狱般的恼怒的解药。

vocab.def_en: Clever, original, and inventive
vocab.def_zh: 巧妙的;有独创性的;机灵的
vocab.quote_en: His smartness of the morning had seemed to Tom a good joke before, and very ingenious.
vocab.quote_zh: 对他上午的那种聪明劲儿，汤姆原先只觉得是个玩笑，而且非常巧妙。
vocab.ex_en: Necessity is the mother of ingenious invention.
vocab.ex_zh: 需要是巧妙发明之母。

vocab.def_en: The quality of being clever, original, and inventive
vocab.quote_en: And now the tiresome chirping of a cricket that no human ingenuity could locate began.
vocab.quote_zh: 接着，一个蟋蟀疲惫的鸣声响了起来，再聪明的人也弄不清是从哪里传来的。
vocab.ex_en: Human ingenuity knows no bounds, but wisdom must guide its application.
vocab.ex_zh: 人类的独创性没有界限，但智慧必须引导其应用。

vocab.def_en: Lacking flavor; lacking vigor or interest
vocab.def_zh: 乏味的;枯燥的;无生气的
vocab.quote_en: he had to talk so properly that speech was become insipid in his mouth.
vocab.quote_zh: 他不得不字斟句酌地讲话，话儿在他嘴里变得十分无趣。
vocab.ex_en: An insipid life is safe but never satisfying.
vocab.ex_zh: 乏味的生活安全但从不令人满足。

vocab.def_en: Unable to be touched; not having physical presence
vocab.def_zh: 无形的;触摸不到的;难以捉摸的
vocab.quote_en: she swung downward and clawed at the intangible air.
vocab.quote_zh: 她晃悠悠地往下，爪子胡乱地抓着无形的空气。
vocab.ex_en: The most valuable things in life are intangible: love, trust, peace.
vocab.ex_zh: 生命中最珍贵的东西是无形的：爱、信任、和平。

vocab.def_en: To insert or introduce something at intervals
vocab.quote_en: He kept tally of the details of the prayer, unconsciously—for he was not listening, but he knew the ground of old, and the clergyman's regular route over it—and when a little trifle of new matter was interlarded, his ear detected it and his whole nature resented it.
vocab.quote_zh: 他下意识地数着祷文的细节——因为他没在听，但他早就熟悉了那些老生常谈和牧师惯常的路线——每当里面夹杂了哪怕一丁点儿新鲜内容，他的耳朵就会捕捉到，他从心底里讨厌这些新内容。
vocab.ex_en: A good story interlards truth with fiction to reveal deeper truth.
vocab.ex_zh: 好故事用虚构穿插真理，以揭示更深的真理。

vocab.def_en: The rise and fall of the voice in speaking
vocab.quote_en: unconsciously to himself his Sunday school voice had acquired a peculiar intonation which was wholly absent on weekdays.
vocab.quote_zh: 不知不觉中，他在主日学校时的讲话语音语调已经变得很特别，与平时大不相同。
vocab.ex_en: Intonation can transform words; the same sentence can bless or curse depending on how it's spoken.
vocab.ex_zh: 语调可以改变言语；同一句话，怎么说可以祝福也可以诅咒。

vocab.def_en: Fearless; adventurous
vocab.quote_en: She had thought that of course Tom had deserted long ago, and she wondered at seeing him place himself in her power again in this intrepid way.
vocab.quote_zh: 她当然以为汤姆早就扔下活儿开溜了，却没料到他居然会如此无畏地重新出现在她面前。
vocab.ex_en: The intrepid heart finds adventure where others see only danger.
vocab.ex_zh: 无畏的心在别人只看到危险的地方发现冒险。

vocab.def_en: A flood; an overwhelming abundance
vocab.quote_en: they could scarcely bail out the cellars under their tongues fast enough to prevent an inundation.
vocab.quote_zh: 他们几乎来不及舀干他们舌头下面的地窖，以防止洪水泛滥。
vocab.ex_en: An inundation of kindness can drown the fires of resentment.
vocab.ex_zh: 善意的洪水可以淹没怨恨之火。

vocab.def_en: Having a particular habit long established; habitual
vocab.def_zh: 根深蒂固的;习惯性的;积习的
vocab.quote_en: She was an inveterate experimenter in these things.
vocab.quote_zh: 在这些事情上，她是个积习难改的实验者。
vocab.ex_en: Hope is an inveterate companion, refusing to leave even when all seems lost.
vocab.ex_zh: 希望是个顽固的伴侣，即使一切似乎都失去了也不肯离开。

vocab.def_en: In a manner showing uncertainty or hesitation
vocab.def_zh: 犹豫不决地;优柔寡断地
vocab.quote_en: Presently she gave over skylarking, and moved irresolutely about, sighing once or twice and glancing furtively and wistfully toward Tom.
vocab.quote_zh: 不一会儿，她不再嬉闹，而是犹豫不决地走来走去，不时叹一口气，偷偷地朝汤姆看一眼。
vocab.ex_en: The irresolute wait for signs while the resolute create them.
vocab.ex_zh: 犹豫不决的人等待迹象，果断的人创造迹象。

vocab.def_en: Tired, bored, or lacking enthusiasm, typically after too much of something
vocab.quote_en: Early in the forenoon parties of jaded men began to straggle into the village, but the strongest of the citizens continued searching.
vocab.quote_zh: 刚到中午，就有一群群的精疲力竭的人开始艰难地回到村子，但是一些最强壮的村民依然在搜寻。
vocab.ex_en: A jaded palate cannot taste the simplest joys.
vocab.ex_zh: 腻烦的味蕾尝不出最简单的快乐。

vocab.def_en: Feeling or expressing great happiness and triumph
vocab.def_zh: 欢欣鼓舞的;喜气洋洋的;欢呼的
vocab.quote_en: The pirates returned to camp. They were jubilant with vanity over their new grandeur and the illustrious trouble they were making.
vocab.quote_zh: 海盗们回到了营地。他们为自己新的辉煌和他们制造的巨大麻烦而欢欣鼓舞，得意洋洋。
vocab.ex_en: The jubilant heart sings even in silence.
vocab.ex_zh: 欢欣鼓舞的心即使在沉默中也在歌唱。

vocab.def_en: Of or relating to a judge or judgment; careful consideration
vocab.quote_en: And above it all the great man sat and beamed a majestic judicial smile upon all the house, and warmed himself in the sun of his own grandeur—for he was "showing off," too.
vocab.quote_zh: 而在这一切之上，端坐着那位大人物，面对一屋子的人，流露着威严的法官般的笑容，沐浴在他自己的显赫地位的温暖阳光里——因为他也在"作秀"。
vocab.ex_en: A judicial mind weighs evidence before reaching conclusions.
vocab.ex_zh: 审慎的头脑在得出结论之前会权衡证据。

vocab.def_en: A complicated network of winding passages; a maze
vocab.def_zh: 迷宫;曲径;错综复杂的事物
vocab.quote_en: for McDougal's Cave was but a vast labyrinth of crooked aisles that ran into each other and out again and led nowhere.
vocab.quote_zh: 因为迈克道格尔岩洞只是个由弯弯曲曲的小径形成的大迷宫，这些小径相互交错然后又不知通向哪里。
vocab.ex_en: The human heart is a labyrinth where even the owner sometimes loses the way.
vocab.ex_zh: 人心是一座迷宫，有时连主人也会迷路。

vocab.def_en: To tear or cut deeply; to wound or hurt
vocab.quote_en: At recess Tom continued his flirtation with Amy with jubilant self-satisfaction. And he kept drifting about to find Becky and lacerate her with the performance.
vocab.quote_zh: 课间休息时，汤姆带着欢快的自我满足，继续向阿米献殷勤。他始终不停地寻找贝姬，用他的表演来伤害她。
vocab.ex_en: Words can lacerate the soul more deeply than any knife can cut the flesh.
vocab.ex_zh: 言语撕裂灵魂，比任何刀子割肉都更深。

vocab.def_en: A person who makes slow progress and falls behind
vocab.def_zh: 迟钝的人;落后者;慢吞吞的人
vocab.quote_en: The congregation being fully assembled now, the bell rang once more, to warn laggards and stragglers.
vocab.quote_zh: 现在，会众全部到齐了，钟又敲响了一次，提醒迟到者和待在外面的人。
vocab.ex_en: The laggard misses opportunities not because they pass too quickly, but because he moves too slowly.
vocab.ex_zh: 落后者错过机会不是因为它们过得太快，而是因为他走得太慢。

vocab.def_en: In a manner lacking energy or enthusiasm; slowly and sluggishly
vocab.def_zh: 懒洋洋地;无精打采地;慢吞吞地
vocab.quote_en: Most of the pupils glanced up languidly, but there were two among them that watched his movements with intent eyes.
vocab.quote_zh: 大多数的学生没精打采地抬头看了一眼，但其中有两个人专注地看着他的动作。
vocab.ex_en: Time flows languidly when we are bored, yet rushes when we are engaged.
vocab.ex_zh: 无聊时时间流得慢，投入时时间过得快。

vocab.def_en: Praise; commendation
vocab.quote_en: he almost forgot the nearly intolerable discomfort of his new clothes in the entirely intolerable discomfort of being set up as a target for everybody's gaze and everybody's laudations.
vocab.quote_zh: 在成为众人目光的焦点和众人赞颂的目标这种完全难以忍受的不适中，他几乎忘记了新衣服那几乎难以忍受的不舒服。
vocab.ex_en: Laudation freely given lifts both the giver and receiver.
vocab.ex_zh: 自由给予的赞美提升给予者和接受者双方。

vocab.def_en: A lack of energy and enthusiasm; sluggishness
vocab.quote_en: Becky roused up from her lethargy of distress, and showed good interest in the proceedings.
vocab.quote_zh: 贝姬从痛苦的无精打采中振作起来，对事态的发展表现出浓厚的兴趣。
vocab.ex_en: Lethargy is the soul's hibernation, waiting for spring to wake it.
vocab.ex_zh: 没精打采是灵魂的冬眠，等待春天唤醒它。

vocab.def_en: Clear and easy to understand; rational
vocab.def_zh: 清晰的;明白的;头脑清楚的
vocab.quote_en: In a lucid interval, Huck feebly led up to the subject of taverns, and finally asked—dimly dreading the worst—if anything had been discovered at the Temperance Tavern since he had been ill.
vocab.quote_zh: 在一个短暂清醒的间歇，哈克无力地提到客栈的话题，最后问道——隐约地为最糟糕的结果担忧——自从他病了之后，客栈里是不是有了什么发现。
vocab.ex_en: A lucid moment can illuminate a lifetime of confusion.
vocab.ex_zh: 一个清晰的时刻可以照亮一生的困惑。

vocab.def_en: Looking or sounding sad and dismal; mournful
vocab.quote_en: Presently a dog set up a long, lugubrious howl just outside—within ten feet of them.
vocab.quote_zh: 不一会儿，就在门外，离他们不到十英尺的地方，一条狗发出了一声哀号。
vocab.ex_en: The lugubrious face often hides a heart that has forgotten how to smile.
vocab.ex_zh: 阴郁的脸常常隐藏着一颗忘了怎么笑的心。

vocab.def_en: Very generous or forgiving, especially toward a rival or someone less powerful
vocab.def_zh: 宽宏大量的;慷慨的;高尚的
vocab.quote_en: the Judge said with a fine outburst that it was a noble, a generous, a magnanimous lie—a lie that was worthy to hold up its head and march down through history breast to breast with George Washington's lauded Truth about the hatchet!
vocab.quote_zh: 法官激动地说，那是一个崇高的、慷慨的、宽宏大量的谎言——这样的谎言，完全有理由抬头挺胸地从历史的长廊中走过，足以跟乔治·华盛顿那值得赞颂的关于小斧头的实话比肩！
vocab.ex_en: The magnanimous heart forgives not because the offense is small, but because love is large.
vocab.ex_zh: 宽宏大量的心原谅不是因为冒犯小，而是因为爱大。

vocab.def_en: A person who is killed because of their beliefs; one who suffers for a cause
vocab.quote_en: The window went up, a maid-servant's discordant voice profaned the holy calm, and a deluge of water drenched the prone martyr's remains!
vocab.quote_zh: 窗子拉上去了，一个女用人不和谐的声音亵渎了眼前这神圣的宁静，一大盆水兜头而下，打湿了平卧在地上的烈士的遗体！
vocab.ex_en: Some become martyrs for truth; others for their own pride.
vocab.ex_zh: 有些人为真理成为烈士；有些人为了自己的骄傲。

vocab.def_en: A deep, pensive, and long-lasting sadness
vocab.quote_en: He surveyed the fence, and all gladness left him, and a deep melancholy settled down upon his spirit.
vocab.quote_zh: 他打量着栅栏，所有的高兴劲儿都离他而去，心里只感到深深的悲伤。
vocab.ex_en: Melancholy is the soul's way of processing loss, a necessary season in the heart's calendar.
vocab.ex_zh: 忧郁是灵魂处理失去的方式，是心灵日历上必要的季节。

vocab.def_en: A person's look or manner, especially one of a particular kind indicating their character or mood
vocab.quote_en: Mr. Walters was very earnest of mien, and very sincere and honest at heart.
vocab.quote_zh: 沃尔特斯先生神态非常认真，心地真诚真挚。
vocab.ex_en: The mien reveals what words conceal.
vocab.ex_zh: 神态揭示言语隐藏的东西。

vocab.def_en: Amusement, especially as expressed in laughter
vocab.quote_en: There was a ripple of mirth, which the court checked.
vocab.quote_zh: 全场响起一阵嬉笑声，但是被法庭制止了。
vocab.ex_en: Mirth is the soul's dance, the heart's celebration of being alive.
vocab.ex_zh: 欢笑是灵魂的舞蹈，是心对活着的庆祝。

vocab.def_en: A person who behaves badly or unlawfully; a villain
vocab.quote_en: for plainly this miscreant had sold himself to Satan and it would be fatal to meddle with the property of such a power as that.
vocab.quote_zh: 因为显然这个无赖已经把自己卖给了魔鬼，去管这么一个恶魔的闲事说不定会送命的。
vocab.ex_en: Every miscreant was once a child with dreams; somewhere along the way, the dreams died.
vocab.ex_zh: 每个恶棍曾经都是个有梦想的孩子；在某个地方，梦想死了。

vocab.def_en: A half; either of two equal parts
vocab.quote_en: Tom divided the cake and Becky ate with good appetite, while Tom nibbled at his moiety.
vocab.quote_zh: 汤姆把蛋糕一分为二，贝姬三口两口就吃完了，而汤姆则一点一点地吃着他那一半。
vocab.ex_en: A moiety shared is greater than a whole hoarded.
vocab.ex_zh: 分享的一半比囤积的整份更大。

vocab.def_en: Dull, tedious, and repetitious; lacking in variety
vocab.def_zh: 单调的;乏味的;千篇一律的
vocab.quote_en: For some time there was no noise but the grating sound of the spades discharging their freight of mould and gravel. It was very monotonous.
vocab.quote_zh: 一段时间里，除了铲子挖着土和砾石时发出的刺耳的声音之外，没有其他任何噪声。这声音很单调。
vocab.ex_en: A monotonous life lacks adventure but offers the peace of predictability.
vocab.ex_zh: 单调的生活缺乏冒险，但提供可预测的平静。

vocab.def_en: In a sullen and ill-tempered manner
vocab.quote_en: Tom sulked in a corner and exalted his woes. He knew that in her heart his aunt was on her knees to him, and he was morosely gratified by the consciousness of it.
vocab.quote_zh: 汤姆缩在角落里生气，更增加了自己的苦恼。他知道，姨妈在心里已经向他认输，意识到这一点，他的郁闷中增添了一丝满足。
vocab.ex_en: Those who gaze morosely at yesterday miss the beauty of today.
vocab.ex_zh: 闷闷不乐地凝视昨天的人错过了今天的美丽。

vocab.def_en: An open rebellion against authority
vocab.quote_en: Mutiny was effectually laid to rest for the moment.
vocab.quote_zh: 叛乱暂时被平息下来。
vocab.ex_en: The soul's mutiny against convention often leads to its greatest discoveries.
vocab.ex_zh: 灵魂对常规的反抗常常导致它最伟大的发现。

vocab.def_en: Smart and fashionable
vocab.quote_en: His cap was a dainty thing, his close-buttoned blue cloth roundabout was new and natty, and so were his pantaloons.
vocab.quote_zh: 他戴着一顶精致的帽子，穿一件扣子扣得严严实实的蓝布紧身短上衣，又新又漂亮，裤子也是这样。
vocab.ex_en: Natty attire may impress the eye, but character impresses the soul.
vocab.ex_zh: 时髦的衣着可能吸引眼球，但品格吸引灵魂。

vocab.def_en: The state of being famous or well known for some bad quality or deed
vocab.quote_en: and best of all, the departed were the talk of the whole town, and the envy of all the boys, as far as this dazzling notoriety was concerned.
vocab.quote_zh: 最妙的是，只要一说起这件令人惊奇的、众所周知的事情，这几个失踪的孩子就成了全镇议论的中心，其他男孩子羡慕的对象。
vocab.ex_en: Notoriety is fame's shadow, often mistaken for the thing itself.
vocab.ex_zh: 恶名是名声的影子，常常被误认为是名声本身。

vocab.def_en: The quality of being new, original, or unusual
vocab.quote_en: This new interest was a valued novelty in whistling, which he had just acquired from a negro.
vocab.quote_zh: 这个新的兴趣就是一种新奇的吹口哨的方式，这是他刚从一个黑人那里学来的。
vocab.ex_en: Novelty attracts, but substance retains.
vocab.ex_zh: 新奇吸引人，但实质留住人。

vocab.def_en: A person new to or inexperienced in a field or situation
vocab.quote_en: These novices had never smoked anything before but cigars made of grape-vine, and they "bit" the tongue, and were not considered manly, anyway.
vocab.quote_zh: 这些初学者以前只抽过用葡萄藤做的烟，他们"咬"着舌头，一点都没男子汉的样子。
vocab.ex_en: Every master was once a novice who refused to give up.
vocab.ex_zh: 每个大师都曾是不肯放弃的初学者。

vocab.def_en: To make someone legally or morally bound to do something; to do as a favor
vocab.quote_en: Yet he felt obliged to speak up and say: "Answer the gentleman, Thomas—don't be afraid."
vocab.quote_zh: 但是他觉得自己有义务说话，就说："回答这位先生的问题，托马斯——别害怕。"
vocab.ex_en: Kindness obliges no one but blesses everyone.
vocab.ex_zh: 善意不迫使任何人，但祝福每个人。

vocab.def_en: Extremely unpleasant; repulsive
vocab.def_zh: 可憎的;讨厌的;令人作呕的
vocab.quote_en: Monday morning always found him so, because it began another week's slow suffering in school. He generally began that day with wishing he had had no intervening holiday; it made the going into captivity and fetters again so much more odious.
vocab.quote_zh: 星期一早晨总是如此——因为这意味着他又要在学校熬过漫长的一个星期。一般来说，他在这一天的开头总是希望没有前面的那个礼拜天，因为过了礼拜天后再度回到被关在学校里的日子，更加令人难以忍受。
vocab.ex_en: Comparison is the odious thief that steals contentment.
vocab.ex_zh: 比较是可憎的贼，偷走满足。

vocab.def_en: Giving the impression that something bad or unpleasant is going to happen
vocab.quote_en: It was discomforting to see Huck eying Joe's preparations so wistfully, and keeping up such an ominous silence.
vocab.quote_zh: 看着哈克这么渴望地注视着乔做着离去的准备，始终令人不安地一声不吭，他感到很不舒服。
vocab.ex_en: The ominous cloud may pass without storm, but wisdom prepares.
vocab.ex_zh: 不祥的云可能无风暴而过，但智慧会做准备。

vocab.def_en: Knowing everything
vocab.quote_en: One of those omniscient and awe-inspiring marvels, a detective, came up from St. Louis, moused around, shook his head, looked wise, and made that sort of astounding success which members of that craft usually achieve.
vocab.quote_zh: 一个无所不知、令人敬畏的奇才，一个侦探，从圣路易斯来到了这里，仔细搜查了一圈后，摇摇头，看上去案情在握的样子，取得了他这个行当的人通常都会取得的令人震惊的成功。
vocab.ex_en: Only love claims to be omniscient, and love is often blind.
vocab.ex_zh: 只有爱情自称无所不知，而爱情常常是盲目的。

vocab.def_en: Subjected to harsh and unfair treatment
vocab.quote_en: for the oppressed millions groaning under the heel of European monarchies and Oriental despotisms.
vocab.quote_zh: 为在欧洲君主制度和东方专制的铁蹄下呻吟的受压迫的百万民众。
vocab.ex_en: The oppressed yearn not for revenge but for justice.
vocab.ex_zh: 受压迫者渴望的不是复仇，而是正义。

vocab.def_en: Ostentatiously rich and luxurious
vocab.quote_en: another was a wasteful and opulent gush of "fine language."
vocab.quote_zh: 另一个特色是肆意堆砌"华丽辞藻"。
vocab.ex_en: The most opulent life is empty without love to fill it.
vocab.ex_zh: 没有爱来填充，最富裕的生活也是空的。

vocab.def_en: The pretentious display of wealth or knowledge, designed to attract admiration
vocab.quote_en: then in the spelling class, and got "turned down," by a succession of mere baby words, till he brought up at the foot and yielded up the pewter medal which he had worn with ostentation for months.
vocab.quote_zh: 拼写课他接连拼错了连小孩都会拼的字，落了个倒数第一，把炫耀了没几个月的奖章交了出去。
vocab.ex_en: True worth needs no ostentation; it shines by its own light.
vocab.ex_zh: 真正的价值不需要炫耀；它用自己的光闪耀。

vocab.def_en: In a manner characterized by pretentious display
vocab.quote_en: The crowd fell apart, now, and the Sheriff came through, ostentatiously leading Potter by the arm.
vocab.quote_zh: 现在，人群散开来，治安长官穿过去，惹人瞩目地抓住波特的手臂。
vocab.ex_en: Those who act ostentatiously often have the least to hide and the most to prove.
vocab.ex_zh: 行为招摇的人常常最没什么可隐藏，也最需要证明自己。

vocab.def_en: An outcast
vocab.quote_en: Shortly Tom came upon the juvenile pariah of the village, Huckleberry Finn, son of the town drunkard.
vocab.quote_zh: 不一会儿汤姆遇到了村子里的小弃儿哈克贝里·芬，他是镇上一个酒鬼的儿子。
vocab.ex_en: The pariah often sees truths that the accepted never notice.
vocab.ex_zh: 被社会遗弃者常常看到被接受者从未注意到的真相。

vocab.def_en: Unfair bias in favor of one thing or person; a particular liking
vocab.quote_en: He had thought he loved her to distraction; he had regarded his passion as adoration; and behold it was only a poor little evanescent partiality.
vocab.quote_zh: 他曾经以为他爱她爱得发疯；他曾经把自己的这种激情看成是一种爱慕；谁知这只是一种转瞬即逝、不值一提的偏见。
vocab.ex_en: Partiality blinds us to the worth of what we overlook.
vocab.ex_zh: 偏心使我们看不到被忽视之物的价值。

vocab.def_en: A quality that evokes pity or sadness
vocab.quote_en: He so worked upon his feelings with the pathos of these dreams that he had to keep swallowing—he was so like to choke; and his eyes swam in a blur of water, which overflowed when he winked, and ran down and trickled from the end of his nose.
vocab.quote_zh: 他的感情沉浸在这些伤心的梦魇中，害得他不停地咽着口水，随时都会透不过气来；他的眼眶里饱含着泪水，眼睛一眨就溢出来，从鼻尖上往下掉。
vocab.ex_en: Pathos touches the heart, but action heals it.
vocab.ex_zh: 伤感触动心，但行动治愈心。

vocab.def_en: Lasting or existing for a long or apparently infinite time; enduring
vocab.quote_en: Huckleberry was always dressed in the cast-off clothes of full-grown men, and they were in perennial bloom and fluttering with rags.
vocab.quote_zh: 哈克贝里总是穿着大人的旧衣服，这些衣服终年油汁麻花，破破烂烂。
vocab.ex_en: Hope is perennial, blooming even in winter's coldest ground.
vocab.ex_zh: 希望是终年的，即使在冬天最冷的地里也会开花。

vocab.def_en: Serious and immediate danger
vocab.quote_en: The Black Avenger stood still with folded arms, "looking his last" upon the scene of his former joys and his later sufferings, and wishing "she" could see him now, abroad on the wild sea, facing peril and death with dauntless heart.
vocab.quote_zh: 黑复仇者双手抱胸，一动不动地站在那里，"最后看一眼"曾经给他欢乐、将要令他受苦的地方，希望"她"现在能看见他，在汹涌的海上，以一颗无畏的心，面对危险和死亡。
vocab.ex_en: In every peril lies an opportunity for courage to be born.
vocab.ex_zh: 每个危险中都蕴藏着勇气诞生的机会。

vocab.def_en: To play the part of; to impersonate
vocab.quote_en: for he was personating a steamboat.
vocab.quote_zh: 因为他在模仿一艘汽船。
vocab.ex_en: We all personate roles in life's drama; the art is to play them well.
vocab.ex_zh: 我们在人生这出戏中都扮演角色；艺术在于演好它们。

vocab.def_en: Spreading through every part of something
vocab.quote_en: There was not even a zephyr stirring; the dead noonday heat had even stilled the songs of the birds; nature lay in a trance that was broken by no sound but the occasional far-off hammering of a woodpecker, and this seemed to render the pervading silence and sense of loneliness the more profound.
vocab.quote_zh: 那里一丝风儿都没有；中午时分的酷热甚至让小鸟停止了歌唱；大自然处在昏睡状态，只有远处偶尔传来啄木鸟的笃笃声，而这似乎使得弥漫的寂静更加弥漫，孤独感更加浓郁。
vocab.ex_en: Silence is the pervading language of deep understanding.
vocab.ex_zh: 沉默是深刻理解的弥漫语言。

vocab.def_en: Relating to the study of the shape and size of the skull as a supposed indication of character
vocab.quote_en: She was a subscriber for all the "Health" periodicals and phrenological frauds; and the solemn ignorance they were inflated with was breath to her nostrils.
vocab.quote_zh: 她是所有"健康"期刊和骗人的颅相学杂志的订户；那些期刊里充斥着像煞有介事的愚昧无知，而对她来说却是不可或缺。
vocab.ex_en: We seek phrenological certainties in a world that defies simple measurement.
vocab.ex_zh: 在一个拒绝简单测量的世界里，我们寻找颅相学般的确定性。

vocab.def_en: In a way that seems reasonable or probable
vocab.def_zh: 貌似合理地;看似可信地
vocab.quote_en: Tom got out of the presence as quick as he plausibly could, and after that he complained of toothache for a week, and tied up his jaws every night.
vocab.quote_zh: 汤姆尽快离开了那里，尽可能不引起怀疑，此后一个星期里，他一直叫牙疼，每个晚上都把下巴扎紧。
vocab.ex_en: Truth told plausibly convinces; truth told poorly is doubted.
vocab.ex_zh: 讲得合理的真理让人信服；讲得不好的真理被怀疑。

vocab.def_en: Easily bent; flexible
vocab.quote_en: finally his bare foot rested upon it, his pliant toes closed upon it, and he hopped away with the treasure and disappeared round the corner.
vocab.quote_zh: 最后他的光脚丫子踩在了花儿上面，他用灵活的脚趾夹着这个宝贝，单腿蹦跳着，在拐角那儿消失了。
vocab.ex_en: The pliant mind bends without breaking and learns from every wind.
vocab.ex_zh: 柔韧的心弯曲而不折断，从每阵风中学习。

vocab.def_en: In a slow and clumsy way because of great weight
vocab.quote_en: As he drew near, he slackened speed, took the middle of the street, leaned far over to starboard, and rounded to ponderously and with laborious pomp and circumstance.
vocab.quote_zh: 驶近之后，他放慢了速度，占着路中央，向右侧倾斜，缓慢地转弯，弯子绕得很大，一副十分费力的样子。
vocab.ex_en: Truth moves ponderously at times, but it always arrives.
vocab.ex_zh: 真理有时行动缓慢，但它总会到达。

vocab.def_en: Of the nature of a portent; ominously significant
vocab.def_zh: 预兆性的;不祥的;惊人的
vocab.quote_en: The artist erected a man in the front yard, that resembled a derrick. He could have stepped over the house; but the girl was not hypercritical; she was satisfied with the monster, and whispered: "It's a beautiful man—now make me coming along." Tom drew an hour-glass with a full moon and straw limbs to it and armed the spreading fingers with a portentous fan.
vocab.quote_zh: 画家在前院画了个人，高大得像个起重机似的，一步就可以跨过房子；不过女孩倒一点也不挑剔；她对这个巨人很满意，喃喃道："这个人真漂亮——把我也画上去，画我在走过来。"汤姆画了个沙漏，上面是一轮圆月，添上麦秆四肢，张开的手指里插了一把古里古怪的扇子。
vocab.ex_en: Small events can be portentous, carrying seeds of great change.
vocab.ex_zh: 小事可能是不祥的预兆，携带着大变化的种子。

vocab.def_en: Having great power, influence, or effect
vocab.def_zh: 强有力的;有效的;有影响力的
vocab.quote_en: The potent palm was uplifted to strike again when Tom cried out: "Hold on, now, what 'er you belting me for?—Sid broke it!"
vocab.quote_zh: 而那只有力的巴掌高举着，正要再打下来，这时汤姆叫了起来："住手，你为什么打我？——糖碗是希德打碎的！"
vocab.ex_en: A kind word is more potent than a thousand angry arguments.
vocab.ex_zh: 一句好话比一千个愤怒的论点更有力。

vocab.def_en: Contrary to reason or common sense; utterly absurd
vocab.quote_en: it was simply preposterous that this boy had warehoused two thousand sheaves of Scriptural wisdom on his premises.
vocab.quote_zh: 这个孩子肚子里居然能有两千句圣经课文，这实在是反常的。
vocab.ex_en: What seems preposterous today may be common sense tomorrow.
vocab.ex_zh: 今天看似荒谬的事，明天可能就是常识。

vocab.def_en: Widespread in a particular area at a particular time
vocab.quote_en: He crossed a small "branch" two or three times, because of a prevailing juvenile superstition that to cross water baffled pursuit.
vocab.quote_zh: 他两三回趟过一条小溪，因为当时在儿童里面盛行一种迷信，趟过河水就能摆脱别人的追踪。
vocab.ex_en: Superstition was prevalent among children and slaves in that time and place.
vocab.ex_zh: 在那个时代和地方，迷信在儿童和奴隶中很盛行。

vocab.def_en: Remarkably or impressively great in extent, size, or degree
vocab.quote_en: The middle-aged man turned out to be a prodigious personage: no less a one than the county judge.
vocab.quote_zh: 那个中年人原来是个声名显赫的大人物——决不低于县法官。
vocab.ex_en: The human capacity for love is prodigious, exceeding all measure.
vocab.ex_zh: 人类爱的能力是巨大的，超出所有度量。

vocab.def_en: A person, especially a young one, with exceptional qualities or abilities
vocab.quote_en: There was only one thing wanting to make Mr. Walters' ecstasy complete, and that was a chance to deliver a Bible-prize and exhibit a prodigy.
vocab.quote_zh: 只缺一件事情就能让沃尔特斯先生的狂喜变得十全十美，这就是颁发一本作为奖品的《圣经》并推出一个神童。
vocab.ex_en: Every child is a prodigy in some realm; the task is to find it.
vocab.ex_zh: 每个孩子都是某个领域的天才；任务是找到它。

vocab.def_en: To treat with disrespect; to violate sacred things
vocab.quote_en: The window went up, a maid-servant's discordant voice profaned the holy calm, and a deluge of water drenched the prone martyr's remains!
vocab.quote_zh: 窗子拉上去了，一个女用人不和谐的声音亵渎了眼前这神圣的宁静，一大盆水兜头而下，打湿了平卧在地上的烈士的遗体！
vocab.ex_en: To profane is to destroy what we cannot create.
vocab.ex_zh: 亵渎就是摧毁我们无法创造的东西。

vocab.def_en: Blasphemous or obscene language
vocab.quote_en: He promised to abstain from smoking, chewing and profanity as long as he remained a member.
vocab.quote_zh: 他保证，只要他还是一个会员，就一定不抽烟，不嚼烟，不说渎神的话。
vocab.ex_en: Profanity often masks a poverty of vocabulary, not depth of feeling.
vocab.ex_zh: 粗话常常掩盖词汇的贫乏，而不是感情的深度。

vocab.def_en: Very great or intense; having deep insight
vocab.quote_en: There was not even a zephyr stirring; the dead noonday heat had even stilled the songs of the birds; nature lay in a trance that was broken by no sound but the occasional far-off hammering of a woodpecker, and this seemed to render the pervading silence and sense of loneliness the more profound.
vocab.quote_zh: 那里一丝风儿都没有；中午时分的酷热甚至让小鸟停止了歌唱；大自然处在昏睡状态，只有远处偶尔传来啄木鸟的笃笃声，而这似乎使得弥漫的寂静更加弥漫，孤独感更加浓郁。
vocab.ex_en: In profound silence, we hear the voice of our own soul.
vocab.ex_zh: 在深刻的沉默中，我们听到自己灵魂的声音。

vocab.def_en: To say that a specified thing will happen in the future
vocab.quote_en: Then there was a dispute about who saw the dead boys last in life, and many claimed that dismal distinction, and offered evidences, more or less tampered with by the witness; and when it was ultimately decided who did see the departed last, and exchanged the last words with them, the lucky parties took upon themselves a sort of sacred importance, and were gaped at and envied by all the rest.
vocab.quote_zh: 然后他们发生了争论：是谁最后一个在那两个死去的孩子身前看见他们的，虽然这不是什么值得骄傲的荣誉，但是大家都往自己身上揽，并且提出证据，而那些证据或多或少地被证人篡改过；当最后判定是谁最后看见了那些死者，最后跟他们说过话时，那些幸运者把自己当成了应受尊敬的要人，其他人都目瞪口呆地看着他们，对他们羡慕不已。
vocab.ex_en: To prophesy is easy; to be right is the challenge.
vocab.ex_zh: 预言容易，正确难。

vocab.def_en: To interrupt at intervals
