vocab.quote_en: She did not finish, for by this time she was bending down and punching under the bed with the broom, and so she needed breath to punctuate the punches with.
vocab.quote_zh: 她没能把话说完，因为这时候她正弯着腰，用扫把往床底下捅，边捅还边得喘气。
vocab.ex_en: Laughter punctuates life's serious moments, reminding us not to take ourselves too seriously.
vocab.ex_zh: 笑声不时打断生活的严肃时刻，提醒我们不要太把自己当回事。

vocab.def_en: To feel or show fear; to tremble
vocab.quote_en: Tom quailed. But presently the temptation rose up strong again and the boys agreed to try, with the understanding that they would take to their heels if the snoring stopped.
vocab.quote_zh: 汤姆退缩了。但是不一会儿冒险的诱惑又变得强烈起来，两个男孩同意试一试，两人商定，一旦鼾声停止，他们就拔脚开溜。
vocab.ex_en: Even the brave may quail in the face of unknown terrors.
vocab.ex_zh: 即使在未知的恐惧面前，勇敢的人也可能胆怯。

vocab.def_en: To search thoroughly and roughly
vocab.quote_en: It was also said that the town had been ransacked for this "murderer" (the public are not slow in the matter of sifting evidence and arriving at a verdict), but that he could not be found.
vocab.quote_zh: 另外还据说，为了寻找"凶手"，全镇被搜了一遍（在细查证据和做出裁决这种事情上，公众可不是温吞水），可是凶手没被找到。
vocab.ex_en: Memory ransacks the past for clues to present happiness.
vocab.ex_zh: 记忆彻底搜索过去，寻找现在幸福的线索。

vocab.def_en: Extremely hungry
vocab.quote_en: They came back to camp wonderfully refreshed, glad-hearted, and ravenous; and they soon had the campfire blazing up again.
vocab.quote_zh: 他们格外精神地回到宿营地，格外精神，满心欢喜，同时饿得不行；他们很快又生起了熊熊篝火。
vocab.ex_en: The ravenous appetite for life is the mark of youth, whatever the age.
vocab.ex_zh: 对生活的极度渴望是青春的标志，无论什么年龄。

vocab.def_en: An expression of sharp disapproval or criticism
vocab.quote_en: There was no voice of rebuke; but there were averted eyes; there was a silence and an air of solemnity that struck a chill to the culprit's heart.
vocab.quote_zh: 没有责备的声音；但是有游移的目光；饭桌旁的沉默和严肃的气氛让这个逃夜者心里一阵发凉。
vocab.ex_en: A gentle rebuke from a friend is worth more than flattery from a thousand strangers.
vocab.ex_zh: 朋友温和的责备比一千个陌生人的奉承更有价值。

vocab.def_en: The restoration of friendly relations
vocab.quote_en: He began to hate himself for throwing away the chance Becky had offered for a reconciliation.
vocab.quote_zh: 他开始恨自己，因为是他放弃了贝姬给他的两人和好的机会。
vocab.ex_en: Reconciliation requires courage from both parties, but cowardice from none.
vocab.ex_zh: 和解需要双方的勇气，不需要任何一方的懦弱。

vocab.def_en: The emblems or insignia of royalty or an organization; splendid clothes
vocab.quote_en: They tramped gaily along, over decaying logs, through tangled underbrush, among solemn monarchs of the forest, hung from their crowns to the ground with a drooping regalia of grapevines.
vocab.quote_zh: 他们高高兴兴，腾腾腾地往前走，跨过腐烂的原木，穿过纠结的下层灌木，行走在威严的森林之王中间，葡萄藤威风凛凛地从这些树中之王的王冠上一直垂落到地上。
vocab.ex_en: True nobility needs no regalia; it wears itself in every gesture.
vocab.ex_zh: 真正的贵族不需要礼服；它在每个姿态中展现自己。

vocab.def_en: Great enjoyment; pleasurable appreciation
vocab.quote_en: The minister gave out the hymn, and read it through with a relish, in a peculiar style which was much admired in that part of the country.
vocab.quote_zh: 牧师诵读赞美诗，整篇赞美诗被他读得有滋有味，在那个地区，他的这种特殊的诵读风格是颇受赞赏的。
vocab.ex_en: Relish the small joys; they are the bricks of happiness.
vocab.ex_zh: 享受小小的快乐；它们是幸福的砖块。

vocab.def_en: A meeting at an agreed time and place
vocab.quote_en: Three miles below St. Petersburg, at a point where the Mississippi River was a trifle over a mile wide, there was a long, narrow, wooded island, with a shallow bar at the head of it, and this offered well as a rendezvous.
vocab.quote_zh: 圣彼得堡南面三英里处的一个地方，密西西比河只有一英里宽一点，那里有一个狭长的、树木茂盛的岛，岛的顶端有一个浅沙洲，那里正好做他们的碰头地点。
vocab.ex_en: The heart has its secret rendezvous with memory, where past and present meet.
vocab.ex_zh: 心灵与记忆有秘密的约会，过去与现在在那里相遇。

vocab.def_en: To feel or express sincere regret about one's wrongdoing
vocab.quote_en: She stood about, restless and uneasy, for a while, glancing at the door, every now and then, hoping she would repent and come to find him.
vocab.quote_zh: 他忐忑不安地在门外站了一会儿，不断地朝门里张望，希望她会后悔，出来找他。
vocab.ex_en: To repent is to turn around and face a new direction.
vocab.ex_zh: 悔改就是转身，面对新的方向。

vocab.def_en: Expressing discontent; fretting
vocab.quote_en: Tom had been restless and full of chafings and repinings; conscience-smitten, too—he could not meet Amy Lawrence's eye.
vocab.quote_zh: 汤姆一直坐立不安，不断地讲废话，发牢骚；同时又感到心虚——他不敢接触阿米·劳伦斯的目光。
vocab.ex_en: Repining changes nothing but the temper of the one who repines.
vocab.ex_zh: 抱怨改变不了什么，只会改变抱怨者的心情。

vocab.def_en: Calm and quiet; restful
vocab.quote_en: Cardiff Hill, beyond the village and above it, was green with vegetation, and it lay just far enough away to seem a Delectable Land, dreamy, reposeful, and inviting.
vocab.quote_zh: 村子远处高高耸立的加迪夫山上草木葱茏，远远望去，它就像一个世外桃源，朦胧，静谧，令人神往。
vocab.ex_en: A reposeful mind finds rest even in chaos.
vocab.ex_zh: 宁静的心即使在混乱中也能找到休息。

vocab.def_en: To restore to life; to bring back into use
vocab.quote_en: She resurrected nothing but the cat.
vocab.quote_zh: 她什么也没捅到，只捅到了一只猫。
vocab.ex_en: Memory can resurrect the dead, if only for a moment.
vocab.ex_zh: 记忆可以复活死者，哪怕只是片刻。

vocab.def_en: A prolongation or reflection of sound; an echo
vocab.quote_en: that wherever one wandered through the maze of passages, lights were to be seen flitting hither and thither in the distance, and shoutings and pistol shots sent their hollow reverberations to the ear down the somber aisles.
vocab.quote_zh: 在迷宫似的小道上，不管走到哪里，都能看见远处闪烁的灯光，听见叫喊声和枪声空洞的回音在忧郁的走道里荡漾。
vocab.ex_en: Kindness has reverberations that echo long after the act is forgotten.
vocab.ex_zh: 善行有回声，在行为被遗忘后久久回荡。

vocab.def_en: Feeling or showing deep and solemn respect
vocab.quote_en: They came by, and stood looking over the paling fence and talking in reverent tones of how Tom did so-and-so the last time they saw him.
vocab.quote_zh: 他们走了过来，站在栅栏边，用崇敬的语气议论着他们最后一次看见汤姆时，他的所作所为。
vocab.ex_en: A reverent heart approaches life with wonder, finding sacred in the ordinary.
vocab.ex_zh: 虔诚的心以惊奇面对生活，在平凡中发现神圣。

vocab.def_en: Keen mental discernment and good judgment; wisdom
vocab.quote_en: She was half sorry her sagacity had miscarried, and half glad that Tom had stumbled into obedient conduct for once.
vocab.quote_zh: 她一方面为自己的聪明没有收到效果略感遗憾，一方面又为汤姆至少这一次表现得老实听话而暗自高兴。
vocab.ex_en: Sagacity sees beyond appearances to the truth beneath.
vocab.ex_zh: 睿智看到表象之下隐藏的真理。

vocab.def_en: The use of irony to mock or convey contempt
vocab.quote_en: Tom tried to think of some way of comforting her, but all his encouragements were grown threadbare with use, and sounded like sarcasms.
vocab.quote_zh: 汤姆试着想办法安慰她，但是他那老一套的鼓劲的话儿毫无新意，听起来就像嘲笑似的。
vocab.ex_en: Sarcasm is the lowest form of wit but the highest form of intelligence when used to expose truth.
vocab.ex_zh: 讽刺是最低级的机智，但当用来揭露真理时是最高级的智慧。

vocab.def_en: To make scratches or small cuts in; to wound with criticism
vocab.quote_en: Tom contrived to scarify the cupboard with it, and was arranging to begin on the bureau, when he was called off to dress for Sunday school.
vocab.quote_zh: 汤姆设法用他的新巴洛刀把碗柜划破，正准备开始对衣柜下手时，被叫去换衣服上主日学校。
vocab.ex_en: Words can scarify the soul more deeply than any blade can cut the flesh.
vocab.ex_zh: 言语割伤灵魂，比任何刀子割肉都更深。

vocab.def_en: An opening in a roof or wall, fitted with a lid
vocab.quote_en: There was a garret above, pierced with a scuttle over his head; and down through this scuttle came a cat, suspended around the haunches by a string.
vocab.quote_zh: 那里有一个阁楼，他头顶上方有一个天窗；一只猫从这天窗里被放下来，腰腿部绑着一根绳子。
vocab.ex_en: Hope is the scuttle through which light enters even the darkest garret of despair.
vocab.ex_zh: 希望是光进入最黑暗的绝望阁楼的天窗。

vocab.def_en: Gloomy and dismal; suggestive of a tomb
vocab.def_zh: 阴森森的;坟墓般的;阴沉的
vocab.quote_en: The deep baying of a hound floated up out of the distance, an owl answered with his sepulchral note.
vocab.quote_zh: 远处传来一条猎狗低沉的吠叫，一只猫头鹰用它那阴森森的叫声应和。
vocab.ex_en: The sepulchral silence of the cave weighed upon the children's spirits.
vocab.ex_zh: 岩洞坟墓般的寂静压在孩子们的心头。

vocab.def_en: A bundle of papers or things gathered together
vocab.quote_en: it was simply preposterous that this boy had warehoused two thousand sheaves of Scriptural wisdom on his premises—a dozen would strain his capacity, without a doubt.
vocab.quote_zh: 这个孩子肚子里居然能有两千句圣经课文，这实在是反常的——其实他撑死了也就知道个十来句。
vocab.ex_en: A sheaf of memories, gathered through life, is the soul's harvest.
vocab.ex_zh: 一生收集的一捆记忆，是灵魂的收获。

vocab.def_en: To swerve or change course quickly
vocab.quote_en: At last the frantic sufferer sheered from its course, and sprang into its master's lap; he flung it out of the window, and the voice of distress quickly thinned away and died in the distance.
vocab.quote_zh: 最后这个发狂的受害者偏离了轨迹，跳上它主人的大腿；主人把它扔出了窗外，悲伤的叫声迅速减弱，并在远处消失了。
vocab.ex_en: Life can sheer in unexpected directions; adaptability is the key to survival.
vocab.ex_zh: 生活可能突然转向意想不到的方向；适应能力是生存的关键。

vocab.def_en: To move sideways, especially in a shy or stealthy manner
vocab.quote_en: Another pause, and more eying and sidling around each other.
vocab.quote_zh: 片刻停顿，相互对视并且兜着圈子。
vocab.ex_en: Truth often sidles into consciousness, arriving not with a bang but a whisper.
vocab.ex_zh: 真理常常悄悄进入意识，不是砰然到来，而是轻声细语。

vocab.def_en: Slightly burned; scorched
vocab.quote_en: "But I forgive ye, Tom. I reckon you're a kind of a singed cat, as the saying is—better'n you look."
vocab.quote_zh: "但是我原谅你，汤姆。我相信你是个俗话说的那种外糙里不糙——心里比外表老实的人。"
vocab.ex_en: A singed heart, once burned by love, learns to approach fire carefully.
vocab.ex_zh: 被爱烧伤过的心，学会小心接近火。

vocab.def_en: Having many curves and turns; winding
vocab.quote_en: They tripped along the murky aisles with the rest of the company, visiting the familiar wonders of the cave—wonders dubbed with rather over-descriptive names, such as "The Drawing Room," "The Cathedral," "Aladdin's Palace," and so on. Presently the hide-and-seek frolicking began, and Tom and Becky engaged in it with zeal until the exertion began to grow a trifle wearisome; then they wandered down a sinuous avenue.
vocab.quote_zh: 他们和其他人一起沿着昏暗的小径走着，参观那些熟悉的岩洞奇观——那些配有夸张名称的奇观，比如"客厅"、"大教堂"、"阿拉丁宫"等等。不一会儿，捉迷藏的游戏开始了，汤姆和贝姬玩得非常投入，直到感觉有点累了，就沿着一条蜿蜒的小路漫步走去。
vocab.ex_en: The path to wisdom is sinuous, with many turnings and backtrackings.
vocab.ex_zh: 通往智慧的道路是蜿蜒的，有许多转弯和回头。

vocab.def_en: To strike with a firm blow
vocab.quote_en: Then his pride was up, and he strode away and went outside. He stood about, restless and uneasy, for a while, glancing at the door, every now and then, hoping she would repent and come to find him. But she did not. Then he began to feel badly and fear that he was in the wrong. It was a hard struggle with him to make new advances, now, but he nerved himself to it and entered. She was still standing back there in the corner, sobbing with her face to the wall. Tom's heart smote him.
vocab.quote_zh: 这时他的自尊心上来了，大步走到门外。他忐忑不安地在门外站了一会儿，不断地朝门里张望，希望她会后悔，出来找他。但是没有。然后他的感觉糟糕起来，害怕自己做错了。现在，要他一切重来，是一场艰苦的斗争，但是他鼓起勇气，走了进去。她依然站在角落里，面朝墙壁，抽泣着。汤姆的心怦怦直跳。
vocab.ex_en: Conscience can smite the soul with blows harder than any hand.
vocab.ex_zh: 良心打击灵魂，比任何手的打击都重。

vocab.def_en: The state or quality of being serious and dignified
vocab.quote_en: The boys talked little, and only under their breath, for the time and the place and the pervading solemnity and silence oppressed their spirits.
vocab.quote_zh: 两个男孩交谈了一下，但都是轻声轻气的，因为彼时彼地，那种渗透性的肃穆和沉寂，令他们情绪低落。
vocab.ex_en: In moments of great solemnity, the soul speaks its deepest truths.
vocab.ex_zh: 在极其庄严的时刻，灵魂说出它最深的真理。

vocab.def_en: To speak one's thoughts aloud when alone
vocab.quote_en: In the afternoon Becky Thatcher found herself moping about the deserted schoolhouse yard, and feeling very melancholy. But she found nothing there to comfort her. She soliloquized: "Oh, if I only had a brass andiron knob again! But I haven't got anything now to remember him by."
vocab.quote_zh: 下午贝姬·撒切尔发现自己没精打采地在空荡荡的学校大院周围转悠，感觉非常忧郁。但是她发现那里没有任何东西可以安慰她。她自言自语道："哦，要是我再有一个壁炉架上的铜把手多好啊！但是现在没有任何东西能让我想到他。"
vocab.ex_en: We all soliloquize in the privacy of our minds; the wise learn to listen.
vocab.ex_zh: 我们都在心灵深处自言自语；智者学会倾听。

vocab.def_en: Loyal, reliable, and hardworking; strong and sturdy
vocab.quote_en: He banged at the door, and presently the heads of the old man and his two stalwart sons were thrust from windows.
vocab.quote_zh: 他砰砰地敲门，老人和他两个健壮的儿子的脑袋很快从窗户伸了出来。
vocab.ex_en: A stalwart friend is worth more than a thousand fair-weather acquaintances.
vocab.ex_zh: 一个坚定的朋友胜过一千个顺境中的熟人。

vocab.def_en: Cautious and surreptitious; intended to escape observation
vocab.def_zh: 偷偷的;秘密的;鬼鬼祟祟的
vocab.quote_en: He climbed the fence, threaded his stealthy way through the plants, till he stood under that window.
vocab.quote_zh: 他翻过栅栏，偷偷摸摸地穿过那些植物，直到站在了那扇窗子底下。
vocab.ex_en: Love's first approaches are often stealthy, afraid of being seen too soon.
vocab.ex_zh: 爱情的最初接近常常是偷偷的，害怕太早被发现。

vocab.def_en: Calm, dependable, and showing little emotion
vocab.def_zh: 不动声色的;麻木的;冷漠的
vocab.quote_en: Now Tom shivered from head to heel; for his eye fell upon the stolid face of Injun Joe.
vocab.quote_zh: 这会儿，汤姆从头到脚都在哆嗦；因为他的目光落在了印第安人乔那张冷漠的脸上。
vocab.ex_en: The stolid face may hide a tempest within.
vocab.ex_zh: 冷漠的脸可能隐藏着内心的风暴。

vocab.def_en: With careful and persistent effort; deliberately
vocab.quote_en: They studiously avoided each other.
vocab.quote_zh: 他们刻意相互回避。
vocab.ex_en: Those who studiously avoid the truth are most likely to stumble over it.
vocab.ex_zh: 刻意回避真理的人最可能被它绊倒。

vocab.def_en: The quality of being sublime; exalted moral or spiritual value
vocab.quote_en: Huckleberry was filled with admiration of Tom's facility in writing, and the sublimity of his language.
vocab.quote_zh: 哈克贝里对汤姆的笔头功夫和用词的高雅佩服得五体投地。
vocab.ex_en: In moments of sublimity, we touch something greater than ourselves.
vocab.ex_zh: 在崇高的时刻，我们触摸到比我们自己更伟大的东西。

vocab.def_en: The sinking or settling to a lower level
vocab.quote_en: But now every sound ceased suddenly, with the subsidence of Mr. Walters' voice, and the conclusion of the speech was received with a burst of silent gratitude.
vocab.quote_zh: 但是，随着沃尔特斯先生的声音的减弱，所有的声音突然停止了，大家以一种突然的沉默，对沃尔特斯终于结束了演讲表示感谢。
vocab.ex_en: After the storm's subsidence comes the peace of calm waters.
vocab.ex_zh: 风暴消退后，是平静水域的安宁。

vocab.def_en: To fail to resist pressure, temptation, or some other negative force
vocab.quote_en: if she felt that way, there was nothing for him to do but succumb.
vocab.quote_zh: 如果她真是这么想的，那他只好屈从。
vocab.ex_en: The wise know when to resist and when to succumb to the inevitable.
vocab.ex_zh: 智者知道何时抵抗，何时向不可避免的事屈服。

vocab.def_en: Damaged or spoiled; tarnished
vocab.quote_en: So they inwardly resolved that so long as they remained in the business, their piracies should not again be sullied with the crime of stealing.
vocab.quote_zh: 于是他们暗下决心，只要他们还从事这个行当，他们的海上抢劫行为就再也不能受到偷窃行为的玷污。
vocab.ex_en: A sullied reputation can be restored; a sullied soul requires deeper cleansing.
vocab.ex_zh: 受损的名声可以恢复；受损的灵魂需要更深层的清洁。

vocab.def_en: In a manner that is splendid and expensive-looking
vocab.quote_en: They were too hungry to stop to fish, but they fared sumptuously upon cold ham, and then threw themselves down in the shade to talk.
vocab.quote_zh: 他们太饿了，没有工夫去钓鱼，而是吞下了大量的冷火腿，然后一头栽倒在阴凉地里，闲聊起来。
vocab.ex_en: Love feasts sumptuously on the simplest offerings.
vocab.ex_zh: 爱情在最简单的奉献上盛宴。

vocab.def_en: The action of asking or begging for something earnestly or humbly
vocab.quote_en: and closed with a supplication that the words he was about to speak might find grace and favor, and be as seed sown in fertile ground, yielding in time a grateful harvest of good.
vocab.quote_zh: 最后，祈求他将要说的话会得到上帝的宽恕和恩典，会像撒在肥沃土地里的种子，到时候获得大丰收。
vocab.ex_en: Supplication is the soul's admission that some things are beyond our power.
vocab.ex_zh: 恳求是灵魂承认有些事情超出了我们的能力。

vocab.def_en: Too long, slow, or dull; tiresome
vocab.def_zh: 冗长的;乏味的;令人厌烦的
vocab.quote_en: Only the older pupils managed to keep their tickets and stick to their tedious work long enough to get a Bible.
vocab.quote_zh: 只有年龄较大的学生才想办法保存他们的票子并且坚持这种单调乏味的努力，直到获得一本《圣经》。
vocab.ex_en: Time spent in tedious labor can yield unexpected fruit.
vocab.ex_zh: 在乏味的劳动中度过的时光可能结出意想不到的果实。

vocab.def_en: Abstinence from alcoholic drink; moderation
vocab.quote_en: Tom joined the new order of Cadets of Temperance, being attracted by the showy character of their "regalia."
vocab.quote_zh: 汤姆加入了新的男生禁酒戒烟会，是因为受到他们引人注目的"制服"的吸引。
vocab.ex_en: Temperance in all things brings balance to life's feast.
vocab.ex_zh: 凡事节制给人生的盛宴带来平衡。

vocab.def_en: Free from disturbance; calm
vocab.quote_en: The sun rose upon a tranquil world, and beamed down upon the peaceful village like a benediction.
vocab.quote_zh: 太阳升起在安宁的地球上，阳光像赐福似的照耀着静谧的村子。
vocab.ex_en: A tranquil mind sees clearly, like still water reflecting the sky.
vocab.ex_zh: 宁静的心看得很清楚，就像静水映照天空。

vocab.def_en: In a peaceful, calm manner
vocab.quote_en: He took up his brush and went tranquilly to work.
vocab.quote_zh: 他拿起刷子，不动声色地干起活来。
vocab.ex_en: Those who live tranquilly disturb no one but inspire all.
vocab.ex_zh: 平静生活的人不打扰任何人，但激励所有人。

vocab.def_en: Beyond ordinary experience; surpassing
vocab.quote_en: She moved like one of those bright beings pictured in the sunny walks of fancy's Eden by the romantic and young, a queen of beauty unadorned save by her own transcendent loveliness.
vocab.quote_zh: 她像浪漫的年轻人想象中那样在梦幻般的伊甸园洒满阳光的小道上行走，一个美丽的王后，除了她本身无与伦比的可爱，没有任何雕饰。
vocab.ex_en: Love is transcendent, reaching beyond time and space.
vocab.ex_zh: 爱是超越的，超越时间和空间。

vocab.def_en: Easy to perceive or detect; obvious
vocab.quote_en: Like many other simple-hearted souls, it was her pet vanity to believe she was endowed with a talent for dark and mysterious diplomacy, and she loved to contemplate her most transparent devices as marvels of low cunning.
vocab.quote_zh: 像许多头脑简单的人一样，她有一种特别的虚荣心，相信自己有一种耍弄神秘莫测手段的天赋，明明是一眼就能看穿的把戏，她总要自以为很了不起，好像没人能解得其中奥秘似的。
vocab.ex_en: A transparent heart hides nothing and fears no scrutiny.
vocab.ex_zh: 透明的心什么也不隐藏，不惧怕任何审视。

vocab.def_en: To travel across or through
vocab.quote_en: At the end of half an hour Tom had a vague general idea of his lesson, but no more, for his mind was traversing the whole field of human thought, and his hands were busy with distracting recreations.
vocab.quote_zh: 半个小时之后，汤姆对自己的功课有了一个模模糊糊的总体印象，但仅此而已，因为他的心思正在穿越人类思想的广袤田野，他的双手正忙着令他分心的消遣。
vocab.ex_en: To traverse difficult terrain is to discover one's own strength.
vocab.ex_zh: 穿越艰难的地形就是发现自己的力量。

vocab.def_en: A thing of little value or importance
vocab.def_zh: 小事;琐事;微不足道的东西
vocab.quote_en: and when a little trifle of new matter was interlarded, his ear detected it and his whole nature resented it; he considered additions unfair, and scoundrelly.
vocab.quote_zh: 每当里面夹杂了哪怕一丁点儿新鲜内容，他的耳朵就会捕捉到，他从心底里讨厌这些新的内容；他认为增加是不公平的，是无赖行为。
vocab.ex_en: Great love is made of a thousand trifles shared.
vocab.ex_zh: 伟大的爱由分享的千百件小事构成。

vocab.def_en: Pure; not mixed with anything else
vocab.quote_en: He felt much as an astronomer feels who has discovered a new planet—no doubt, as far as strong, deep, unalloyed pleasure is concerned, the advantage was with the boy, not the astronomer.
vocab.quote_zh: 他的感觉就像一个天文学家发现了一颗新的星球——毫无疑问，这个孩子比天文学家所要感到的欢乐更由衷、更纯真。
vocab.ex_en: Unalloyed happiness is rare; most joy comes alloyed with care.
vocab.ex_zh: 纯粹的快乐是罕见的；大多数快乐都掺杂着忧虑。

vocab.def_en: Fully in agreement
vocab.quote_en: The spectacle took the general breath away. All gazed, nobody spoke for a moment. Then there was a unanimous call for an explanation.
vocab.quote_zh: 这个景象让所有人喘不过气来。大家都瞪眼看着，一时间没人说话。然后大家一致要求他解释一下。
vocab.ex_en: Unanimous agreement sometimes masks unspoken doubts.
vocab.ex_zh: 一致同意有时掩盖未说出口的疑虑。

vocab.def_en: Not pleasant to taste; unpleasant or unacceptable
vocab.def_zh: 难吃的;令人不快的;无法接受的
vocab.quote_en: But enough of this. Homely truth is unpalatable.
vocab.quote_zh: 但是，大实话是不讨人喜欢的。
vocab.ex_en: The most unpalatable truths are often the most necessary to swallow.
vocab.ex_zh: 最难以下咽的真理常常是最需要咽下的。

vocab.def_en: To find fault with; to scold
vocab.quote_en: So she sat down to cry again and upbraid herself; and by this time the scholars began to gather again, and she had to hide her griefs and still her broken heart.
vocab.quote_zh: 于是她坐下，又哭了起来，并且责骂自己；这时候，同学们又聚拢来，她只好藏起悲伤，让破碎的心安静下来。
vocab.ex_en: To upbraid another is to reveal one's own dissatisfaction with self.
vocab.ex_zh: 责备别人就是暴露对自己的不满。

vocab.def_en: A person who wanders from place to place without a home or job
vocab.def_zh: 流浪者;漂泊者;无业游民
vocab.quote_en: These were strange words to the vagabond boy's ears, and the pleasantest he had ever heard.
vocab.quote_zh: 这些是这个居无定所的孩子听来非常奇怪，也是他听到过的最让他高兴的话。
vocab.ex_en: The vagabond sees what the settled never notice.
vocab.ex_zh: 流浪者看到定居者从未注意的东西。

vocab.def_en: Wandering from place to place; having no fixed home
vocab.quote_en: Presently a vagrant poodle dog came idling along, sad at heart, lazy with the summer softness and the quiet, weary of captivity, sighing for change.
vocab.quote_zh: 不一会儿一条迷路的卷毛狗懒洋洋地走过来，它心里正悲伤着，对夏日的安逸宁静感到无聊，对束缚感到厌烦，渴望改变。
vocab.ex_en: A vagrant thought can lead to the most settled conclusion.
vocab.ex_zh: 一个游荡的念头可以导致最确定的结论。

vocab.def_en: To defeat thoroughly
vocab.quote_en: The children left for school, and the old lady to call on Mrs. Harper and vanquish her realism with Tom's marvelous dream.
vocab.quote_zh: 孩子们上学去了，老太太去拜访哈帕太太，要用汤姆神奇的梦战胜她对现实的信念。
vocab.ex_en: To vanquish an enemy is easy; to vanquish oneself is the greater victory.
vocab.ex_zh: 征服敌人容易；征服自己是更大的胜利。

vocab.def_en: An antechamber or small entrance hall
vocab.quote_en: next the belle of the village, followed by a troop of lawn-clad and ribbon-decked young heart-breakers; then all the young clerks in town in a body—for they had stood in the vestibule sucking their cane-heads, a circling wall of oiled and simpering admirers, till the last girl had run their gauntlet.
vocab.quote_zh: 接下来是村子里的美女，后面跟着一群身穿上等细布衣服，扎着缎带的令人伤心的年轻姑娘；随后一起进来的是镇上所有的年轻职员——他们是那群姑娘的爱慕者，刚才一直站在门厅里，嚼着甘蔗，围成一圈，醉酒似的哧哧傻笑，直到最后一个姑娘逃过他们的夹击。
vocab.ex_en: The vestibule of the mind is where first impressions enter.
vocab.ex_zh: 心灵的门厅是第一印象进入的地方。

vocab.def_en: To annoy, frustrate, or worry
vocab.quote_en: The old lady was vexed to think she had overlooked that bit of circumstantial evidence, and missed a trick.
vocab.quote_zh: 想不到自己忽略了一个无关紧要的证据，就让自己的把戏落空，波莉姨妈很恼火。
vocab.ex_en: Small matters vex small minds; great souls rise above annoyance.
vocab.ex_zh: 小事困扰小心灵；伟大的灵魂超越烦恼。

vocab.def_en: Having a strong desire for revenge
vocab.def_zh: 报复性的;复仇的;怀恨的
vocab.quote_en: She roused up now, with a vindictive cast in her eye, and gave her plaited tails a shake and said she knew what she'd do.
vocab.quote_zh: 她站起来，眼睛里带着报复的神色，晃了一下辫子，说她知道该做什么。
vocab.ex_en: A vindictive heart builds its own prison and throws away the key.
vocab.ex_zh: 报复的心建起自己的监狱并扔掉钥匙。

vocab.def_en: The body's internal organs, especially those essential to life
vocab.quote_en: He had a citified air about him that ate into Tom's vitals.
vocab.quote_zh: 他浑身透着城里人的气派，这最让汤姆受不了。
vocab.ex_en: Kindness touches the vitals of the soul, healing what medicine cannot reach.
vocab.ex_zh: 善意触动灵魂的核心，治愈药物无法触及的地方。

vocab.def_en: Liveliness and high spirits
vocab.quote_en: She said to a girl almost at Tom's elbow—with sham vivacity: "Why, Mary Austin! you bad girl, why didn't you come to Sunday school?"
vocab.quote_zh: 她假装轻快地对几乎就在汤姆肘边的一个女孩说："哟，玛丽·奥斯丁！你这坏姑娘，你为什么不来主日学校上课？"
vocab.ex_en: Vivacity is the soul's dance, the heart's celebration of existence.
vocab.ex_zh: 活泼是灵魂的舞蹈，是心对存在的庆祝。

vocab.def_en: The current fashion or style
vocab.quote_en: However, even inquests went out of vogue at last, and ceased to torture Tom's conscience.
vocab.quote_zh: 然而，就连验尸最后也失去了新鲜劲儿，不再折磨汤姆的良心。
vocab.ex_en: Truth never goes out of vogue, though it may be temporarily out of fashion.
vocab.ex_zh: 真理从不过时，尽管它可能暂时不流行。

vocab.def_en: A person who is devoted to a particular pursuit or way of life
vocab.quote_en: In fancy, the voluptuous votary of fashion sees herself amid the festive throng, "the observed of all observers."
vocab.quote_zh: 在幻觉中，沉溺于追逐时尚的人以为自己置身于节日聚会的人群中，成为"万众瞩目的对象"。
vocab.ex_en: Every artist is a votary at the altar of creation.
vocab.ex_zh: 每个艺术家都是创造祭坛前的献身者。

vocab.def_en: Lacking sophistication or good taste; crude
vocab.quote_en: At last the enemy's mother appeared, and called Tom a bad, vicious, vulgar child, and ordered him away.
vocab.quote_zh: 最后仇敌的妈妈出现了，她骂汤姆是个邪恶、粗鲁的坏孩子，并责令他离开。
vocab.ex_en: That which is truly vulgar is not simple speech, but a mean spirit.
vocab.ex_zh: 真正粗俗的不是简单的言语，而是卑鄙的精神。

vocab.def_en: To decrease in size, extent, or degree
vocab.quote_en: When the interest in art began to wane, the two fell to talking.
vocab.quote_zh: 当画画的兴趣开始减弱后，两个人开始讲起话来。
vocab.ex_en: As the moon wanes only to wax again, so do our fortunes rise and fall.
vocab.ex_zh: 正如月缺还会月圆，我们的命运也是如此起伏。

vocab.def_en: To intercept or attack from ambush
vocab.quote_en: He waylaid other boys as they came, and went on buying tickets of various colors ten or fifteen minutes longer.
vocab.quote_zh: 他拦截了其他的进来的男孩子，换了各种颜色的票子，又花了十五分钟。
vocab.ex_en: Hope waylays despair in the ambush of possibility.
vocab.ex_zh: 希望在可能性的埋伏中拦截绝望。

vocab.def_en: To roll about; to be soaked in
vocab.quote_en: he was weltering in tears again, long before she was through.
vocab.quote_zh: 没等她说完，他早已就又哭成了泪人儿。
vocab.ex_en: The soul may welter in grief, but it can also rise from its depths.
vocab.ex_zh: 灵魂可能沉浸在悲伤中，但它也能从深处升起。

vocab.def_en: To go or proceed on one's way
vocab.quote_en: The boy mused a while over the substantial change which had taken place in his worldly circumstances, and then wended toward headquarters to report.
vocab.quote_zh: 汤姆对发生在自己的世俗境地中的实质性变化琢磨了很久，随后便回总部汇报去了。
vocab.ex_en: As we wend through life, we collect stories like flowers along the path.
vocab.ex_zh: 当我们走过人生，我们收集故事就像收集路边的花。

vocab.def_en: To sharpen or stimulate
vocab.quote_en: The poor morsel of food only whetted desire.
vocab.quote_zh: 这么点儿可怜的食物只是刺激了他们的食欲。
vocab.ex_en: Curiosity whets the appetite for knowledge.
vocab.ex_zh: 好奇心刺激对知识的渴望。

vocab.def_en: Skilled at gaining an advantage, especially deceitfully
vocab.quote_en: These despised themselves, as being the dupes of a wily fraud, a guileful snake in the grass.
vocab.quote_zh: 他们看不起自己，觉得自己就像是被一个狡诈的骗子、草地里一条狡猾的蛇欺骗的人一样。
vocab.ex_en: The wily mind finds shortcuts; the wise mind finds the right path.
vocab.ex_zh: 狡猾的心找捷径；智慧的心找正路。

vocab.def_en: With a feeling of vague or regretful longing
vocab.def_zh: 渴望地;伤感地;依依不舍地
vocab.quote_en: Huckleberry viewed it wistfully. The temptation was very strong.
vocab.quote_zh: 哈克贝里留恋地看着。这个诱惑实在太强烈了。
vocab.ex_en: The wistful gaze toward yesterday teaches us to treasure today.
vocab.ex_zh: 对昨天依依不舍的目光教我们珍惜今天。

vocab.def_en: The highest point reached; the peak
vocab.quote_en: And at the zenith of his fame, how he would suddenly appear at the old village and stalk into church, brown and weather-beaten, in his black velvet doublet and trunks, his great jack-boots, his crimson sash, his belt bristling with horse-pistols, his crime-rusted cutlass at his side, his slouch hat with waving plumes, his black flag unfurled, with the skull and crossbones on it, and hear with swelling ecstasy the whisperings, "It's Tom Sawyer the Pirate!—the Black Avenger of the Spanish Main!"
vocab.quote_zh: 在他声誉达到顶峰时，他会突然出现在老村子里，踏进那座遭受了日晒雨淋的褐色教堂，他会身穿黑丝绒紧身上衣，短衬裤，脚蹬长统靴，披着猩红色肩带，腰带上挂着马枪，腰边挂着锈迹斑斑的短弯刀，阔边帽上饰着摇摆的羽毛，他的黑旗打开，上面有骷髅和交叉的股骨图形，他会听见人们的交头接耳："这是海盗汤姆·索亚！——加勒比海的黑衣复仇侠！"
vocab.ex_en: At the zenith of success, remember the valley from which you climbed.
vocab.ex_zh: 在成功的顶峰，记住你爬出的山谷。

vocab.def_en: A soft, gentle breeze
vocab.quote_en: There was not even a zephyr stirring; the dead noonday heat had even stilled the songs of the birds.
vocab.quote_zh: 那里一丝风儿都没有；中午时分的酷热甚至让小鸟停止了歌唱。
vocab.ex_en: A zephyr of kindness can cool the hottest temper.
vocab.ex_zh: 善意的微风可以冷却最热的脾气。
